Future development should therefore move beyond empirical pan-pathway inhibition toward biomarker-guided, tumor-context-specific precision strategies integrating selective E1, E2, and E3 inhibitors, rational combination regimens, pharmacodynamic monitoring, resistance profiling, immune-state assessment, and tumor-targeted delivery systems.

articles.title: Recent advances in the pharmacological effects and mechanisms of borneol and borneol-containing formulations in central nervous system diseases.
articles.abstract: Borneol is an aromatic medicinal agent widely used in traditional Chinese medicine, both as a standalone component and as an ingredient in multi-herb formulations. Its pharmacological relevance to central nervous system (CNS) disorders has attracted increasing attention, particularly in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, ischemic stroke, and glioma. Accumulating evidence indicates that borneol may influence multiple pathophysiological processes, including brain-barrier function and drug delivery, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, neurotransmitter homeostasis and neuronal excitability, cellular injury and death, and the clearance of pathological substances and post-injury repair. Here, we integrate and compare these mechanisms across disease contexts. Notably, although several actions of borneol appear to converge across CNS disorders, others are strongly disease- and context-dependent; for example, its effects on brain-barrier permeability, oxidative stress, and cell death may differ in direction according to disease pathology and therapeutic intent. Pharmacokinetic studies support measurable brain exposure to borneol, yet direct comparative evidence of pharmacological activity, brain disposition, and human pharmacokinetics among borneol preparations of different botanical origins and stereochemical configurations remains scarce. Borneol-containing formulations also exhibit multi-level pharmacological effects; however, because most studies lack borneol-alone, borneol-depleted, or add-back controls, these effects cannot be unequivocally attributed to borneol itself. Overall, the current evidence base remains dominated by cellular and animal studies, with several proposed mechanisms inferred primarily from changes in molecular expression or computational predictions. Robust causal validation, high-quality clinical evidence, and long-term safety data are still limited. Future studies should therefore define the dose-exposure-response relationships and disease-specific therapeutic windows of different borneol preparations, establish the independent contribution of borneol within complex formulations, and determine its genuine therapeutic value and long-term safety through rigorous mechanistic and clinical investigation.

articles.title: Endolysins for precision antimicrobial therapy and rapid bacterial detection: translational challenges and future directions.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of alternative therapeutic and diagnostic strategies. Among emerging approaches, bacteriophage-derived endolysins have attracted considerable attention as promising tools for combating bacterial infections. Endolysins are phage-encoded peptidoglycan-degrading enzymes that have shown significant potential for both antimicrobial and diagnostic applications against a wide range of bacterial pathogens. This review summarizes the current knowledge of endolysins, highlighting their rapid bacteriolytic activity, high target specificity, and diverse therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Beyond their antimicrobial potential, endolysin-derived cell wall-binding domains (CBDs) and phage receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) have emerged as highly specific recognition molecules for the rapid detection of bacterial pathogens in clinical diagnostics and food safety. Rapid and accurate pathogen detection is essential for timely disease management, infection control, and the prevention of foodborne contamination. Despite these promising attributes, several challenges continue to limit the clinical and industrial translation of endolysins, including constraints related to protein expression, stability, formulation, and large-scale production. Furthermore, the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria remains a major obstacle to endolysin activity by restricting access to the peptidoglycan layer. Recent advances in protein engineering, membrane-permeabilization strategies, and delivery approaches have provided promising solutions to overcome these limitations. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the current advances, translational challenges, and future prospects of engineered endolysins as precision antimicrobial agents and diagnostic tools for combating antimicrobial-resistant bacterial pathogens.

articles.title: Threshold-triggered microneedle applicators: converting user-applied force into reproducible dissolving microneedle insertion for global vaccination.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccine distribution in low- and middle-income countries is constrained by healthcare workforce shortages - averaging one health worker per 435 people - and by unreliable facility infrastructure. Dissolving microneedle patches address these bottlenecks by reducing cold-chain reliance and enabling dose-sparing immunization through skin-resident antigen-presenting cells. However, reproducible administration by minimally trained personnel remains a critical barrier to deployment. AREA COVERED: This review examines five representative applicator architectures from the peer-reviewed and patent literature, detailing how each converts variable user input into a standardized, high-velocity impact that overcomes rate-dependent skin viscoelasticity to ensure deep, reproducible stratum corneum penetration. Each is evaluated against three prerequisites for global deployment: sufficient insertion force and rate, low-cost manufacturability, and power independence. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Patents were searched from 2004 to June 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Validation remains weighted toward mechanical and ex vivo testing, so the field's engineering maturity runs ahead of its translational readiness. Realizing the public health potential of microneedle vaccines will require user-independent operation, scalable manufacturing, and integration of threshold-triggered mechanisms with patch design so that delivered dose and immune response are reproducible. Eliminating pre-loaded energy components is central to the cost competitiveness that mass immunization in resource-limited settings demands.

articles.title: Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction ameliorates gastric mucosal injury in chronic gastritis with liver-stomach disharmony syndrome through the gut microbiota-hepatic bile acid metabolism axis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic gastritis (CG) is a high-incidence disease in the digestive system, and liverstomach disharmony syndrome (LSD) is a relatively common syndrome type. This study aimed to evaluate the role and possible mechanism of traditional Chinese medicine Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction (WMS) in treating LSDCG. METHODS: The CG and LSDCG animal models were established and treated with WMS to observe the TCM syndrome scores and behavioral changes, histopathological alterations of the gastric mucosa, and expressions of pro-inflammatory cytokines and tight junction proteins. Then, the changes of gut microbiota and bile acids (BAs) were analyzed by microbiota sequencing and mass spectrometry, and the protein expressions of BA receptors were detected by immunohistochemistry and WB. Finally, Lgr5-positive (Lgr5+) gastric cells were observed by immunofluorescence staining, the expression of gastric mucosal cell differentiation markers was detected by RT-qPCR, and the fatty acid oxidation (FAO) of Lgr5+ cells was observed by fluorescence double staining. RESULTS: WMS reduced the TCM syndrome scores, increased the autonomous activity ability, and improved gastric mucosal injury, inflammatory response, and gastric mucosal barrier disruption in the CG and LSDCG model rats. WMS also regulated the intestinal microbiota and BA metabolism of model rats, and promoted the levels of PPARα and RXR. In addition, WMS attenuated the loss of Lgr5+ gastric stem cells and promoted their differentiation and FAO. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, WMS promoted the differentiation of Lgr5+ gastric stem cells, potentially involving the gut microbiotahepatic BA metabolism axis to repair gastric mucosal injury in LSDCG.

articles.title: Spartina anglica extract attenuates TNF-α/IFN-γ-induced inflammatory responses in HaCaT keratinocytes through suppression of the MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT1 signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Spartina anglica extract (SAE) in a human keratinocyte model of inflammation. HaCaT cells were stimulated with tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) to induce inflammatory responses. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay to determine non-cytotoxic concentrations. The expression of the chemokines TARC/CCL17 and macrophage-derived chemokine MDC/CCL22 was quantified at both the mRNA and protein levels using quantitative real-time PCR and ELISA, respectively. In addition, the activation of key inflammatory signaling pathways was evaluated by Western blot analysis. SAE did not exhibit cytotoxic effects at concentrations up to 250 μg/mL. Under inflammatory conditions, SAE significantly reduced the expression of CCL17 and CCL22 in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, this suppression was associated with decreased phosphorylation of MAPK signaling components, including ERK, JNK, and p38, as well as inhibition of NF-κB and STAT1 activation. High-performance liquid chromatography analysis revealed a major peak corresponding to the retention time of iso-orientin in SAE. These findings suggest that SAE may attenuate keratinocyte-mediated inflammatory responses through modulation of chemokine expression and key intracellular signaling pathways.

articles.title: Machine-learning-assisted target prioritization and experimental validation of the neoeriocitrin-mTOR axis in impaired osteogenic differentiation.
articles.abstract: Neoeriocitrin (NEO) is a citrus-derived flavonoid with potential osteoprotective activity, but its pharmacological targets and mechanisms in impaired osteogenic differentiation remain unclear. Osteoporosis-related differentially expressed genes were intersected with predicted NEO targets, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest, and support vector machine analyses consistently prioritized MTOR for mechanistic investigation. Molecular docking predicted a favorable binding pose of NEO at the 12-kDa FK506-binding protein (FKBP12)-mTOR FKBP12-rapamycin-binding (FRB) interface, while the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) demonstrated increased cellular thermal stability of mTOR following NEO treatment, supporting an mTOR-associated intracellular effect. In dexamethasone-treated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, NEO dose-dependently restored alkaline phosphatase activity, mineralized nodule formation, and the expression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), osteopontin (OPN), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP). NEO also enhanced autophagic flux, increased the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B)-II/LC3B-I ratio, reduced p62 expression, and suppressed dexamethasone-induced phosphorylation of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1 (S6K1). Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy with 3-methyladenine (3-MA) and mTOR overexpression both attenuated the pro-osteogenic effects of NEO. Collectively, these findings support an mTORC1-associated S6K1 signaling mechanism linking NEO treatment to autophagy regulation and osteogenic differentiation. NEO may therefore represent a candidate natural compound for further preclinical investigation in osteoporosis-related bone loss.

articles.title: An immune-resistance dual-axis framework prioritizes MAL2 for functional investigation in lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped lung cancer treatment, yet durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients. Biomarkers incompletely capture interactions between immune activation and tumor-intrinsic resistance. Integrating immune and epithelial expression programs may help identify response-associated states and candidates for functional investigation. METHODS: Public bulk transcriptomes were analyzed with format-specific preprocessing, empirical Bayes differential expression, standardized cross-cohort evidence, and gene-set enrichment. Five discovery-informed modules formed an immune-resistance score. Conditional leave-one-out and leave-cohort-out analyses refitted normalization within training data and compared the fixed score with a nested ridge-logistic model. Survival, composition-adjustment, and prioritization sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell counts underwent quality control, unsupervised clustering, and patient-level pseudobulk analysis. MAL2 was investigated in A549 and H1299 cells using knockdown, growth, motility, apoptosis, HLA-ABC, cytokine, and PBMC co-culture assays. RESULTS: No individual gene met FDR <0.05 in any of the three discovery contrasts. Favorable-response genes were enriched for adaptive immune processes, whereas the unfavorable list showed weaker DNA-replication enrichment. Conditional leave-cohort-out AUCs for the dual-axis score were 0.964, 0.859, and 0.773; performance did not consistently exceed the immune axis. In GSE190266, outcome analysis yielded a cohort-relative AUC of 0.617 with incomplete module coverage. Higher scores were associated with longer PFS in two evaluated cohorts. Quality control retained 91,762 single cells. MAL2 remained epithelial-enriched and ranked third among 58 evaluable candidates, but its patient-level epithelial response contrast and standalone PFS associations were not significant. Knockdown reduced growth and motility-related readouts, increased apoptosis and HLA-ABC expression, and altered cytokine and co-culture activation readouts. CONCLUSION: The immune-resistance framework links cohort-level response patterns to epithelial candidates for functional investigation. MAL2 depletion alters growth and immune-related phenotypes in lung cancer cells, supporting further investigation of its biological role.

articles.title: Safety evaluation of genipin in Beagle dogs: acute and 28-day repeated oral toxicity studies.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Genipin, a typical iridoid constituent derived from the fruits of Gardenia jasminoides Ellis, is an essential in vivo metabolite of geniposide. It exhibits diverse potent biofunctions, including hepatoprotection, anti-inflammation, neuroprotection, antioxidation, and glycolipid metabolism modulation. Nevertheless, the systemic toxicological profile of genipin remains insufficiently characterized, with particularly limited safety evidence from non-rodent models. This study aimed to evaluate the acute and subacute oral toxicity of genipin in Beagle dogs as a preclinical safety assessment. METHODS: Acute toxicity was assessed using single oral doses of genipin at 29, 41, 59, 84, 120, and 140 mg/kg. For subacute toxicity, repeated-dose groups were administered 3, 9, and 27 mg/kg/day for 28 days. Clinical signs, body weight, food intake, hematology, clinical chemistry, urinalysis, electrocardiography, fecal occult blood, and histopathology were evaluated. RESULTS: The results showed that the oral approximate lethal dose of genipin was 120.0-140.0 mg/kg, with doses ≥41 mg/kg inducing thymic, hepatorenal, and gallbladder toxicity. Repeated 27 mg/kg/day genipin caused gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, prolonged coagulation parameters, and toxicity to the hepatobiliary system, thymus, bone marrow, and gonads; 3 and 9 mg/kg/day genipin induced mild male gonad toxicity. Bone marrow toxicity and gastric mucosal irritation were fully reversible after recovery, while hepatic, thymic, and gonadal toxicity showed partial recovery. CONCLUSION: This study clarified the dose-toxicity relationship, major target organs, and toxic reversibility of genipin following oral exposure in non-rodent species. These findings provide robust preclinical toxicological evidence to support rational dosage optimization, risk assessment, and the safe use of genipin.

articles.title: An Integrated Network of Classical Endocrine and Retinoic Acid Pathways Reveals Points of Convergence and Knowledge Gaps.
articles.abstract: Adverse outcome pathways (AOPs) are pragmatic descriptions of how molecular perturbations can lead to adverse effects in intact organisms. To examine connectivity across endocrine signalling pathways, we integrated 117 AOPs related to oestrogen, androgen, steroidogenesis, thyroid and retinoic acid (EATS,R) modalities into a unified endocrine AOP network (AOPN). The resulting network revealed uneven pathway representation, limited mechanistic integration across EATS,R modalities and substantial gaps in certain signalling coverage, with only six retinoic acid-related AOPs available for integration. At the same time, the AOPN identified highly connected biological nodes linking multiple pathways to adverse outcomes, highlighting potential points of endocrine crosstalk as well as cross-species key events (KEs), bridging human and environmental health. To strengthen retinoid pathway integration, new KEs describing altered retinoic acid receptor activation were developed as potential network hubs (KE 2419 and KE 2420). Collectively, these findings demonstrate how the AOPN reveals emergent biological relationships, exposes knowledge gaps and identifies candidate targets for NAM development, providing a framework that could be used to prioritise future AOP development, and overall, to support a more integrated, system-level approach to endocrine disruptor identification.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction of Protein Kinase-Ligand Binding Affinity Using Extended Connectivity Interaction Features.
articles.abstract: Protein kinases are key cellular regulators of growth, proliferation, and signal transduction, making them important therapeutic targets in precision medicine, particularly for cancer and inflammatory diseases. Although molecular docking remains a central tool in structure-based drug discovery, its predictive accuracy is often limited by rigid receptor assumptions and simplified solvent representation. To overcome these limitations, machine learning models were developed based on Extended Connectivity Interaction Features to predict kinase-ligand binding affinities. A kinase-specific dataset of 2,337 complexes from PDBbind 2020 was used to train five regression models, namely Decision Tree, Support Vector Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, using a merged descriptor set of 1,757 interaction-specific and physicochemical features. Integration of RDKit descriptors consistently improved predictive performance across models. Among the evaluated models, GBR achieved the highest predictive correlation, with a PCC of 0.72 and R2 value of 0.51, while SVR yielded the lowest mean squared error value of 0.84 with a PCC of 0.71. The XGBoost and RF followed with R2 values of 0.49 and 0.42, respectively, whereas DT showed the weakest performance, with an R2 value of 0.25 and a PCC of 0.54. External validation on 5,265 complexes further confirmed the robustness of the framework and facilitated the identification of high-confidence binding candidates through consensus prediction. Notably, this strategy accurately predicted binding affinities and enabled prioritization of the top 20 compounds as potential kinase-binding leads, demonstrating a scalable and computationally efficient framework for improved virtual screening and hit prioritization in rational drug discovery.

articles.title: Sertraline disassembles the mitochondrial transduceosome and disrupts testosterone biosynthesis.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) sertraline is limited by its frequent side effect of sexual dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate how sertraline directly disrupts testicular testosterone synthesis. Using an integrated approach combining network toxicology, molecular docking, in-vivo mouse model, and in-vitro Leydig cells experiments, we identified that clinical doses of sertraline significantly suppressed testosterone synthesis. Mechanistically, sertraline downregulated the protein level of the steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR), the rate-limiting enzyme for testosterone synthesis, without affecting its mRNA level. Molecular docking and thermal shift assays revealed that sertraline specifically binds to the outer mitochondrial membrane protein VDAC1 with high affinity. This binding site spatially overlapped with the StAR-VDAC1 interaction interface. Consequently, sertraline disrupted the formation of the StAR-VDAC1 transduceosome, as validated by co-immunoprecipitation analysis. This led to StAR destabilization and degradation, thereby blocking mitochondrial cholesterol import and subsequently testosterone biosynthesis. Crucially, VDAC1 overexpression rescued sertraline-induced downregulation of StAR and restored testosterone synthesis. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that sertraline disrupts testosterone synthesis by binding to VDAC1, disrupting the essential StAR-VDAC1 interaction and leading to StAR degradation. This mechanism provides a new perspective for understanding the clinical reproductive-related side effects of sertraline and for developing intervention strategies targeting the VDAC1-StAR interaction.

articles.title: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. stem extract attenuates cigarette smoke-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in mice by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (COT) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its root, stem, and leaf being used for medicinal purposes. COT characterized by the efficacy of dispelling wind-dampness, invigorating blood, and relieving pain, traditional records in Quanzhou Bencao document the use for asthma, indicating that its traditional treatment in lung system disorders. Previous pharmacological studies have demonstrated that the COT stem (COTS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and protective effects in experimental models related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the systemically efficacy and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-COPD effects of COTS remain poorly understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: The purpose of this study is to systematically investigate the therapeutic efficacy of the extract of COTS (ECOTS) against COPD in mice through metabolomics and serum pharmacochemistry combined with network pharmacology, thereby providing experimental evidence for elucidating the underlying mechanisms through which ECOTS exerts its therapeutic effects on COPD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD-like mouse model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of ECOTS. The potential biomarkers were identified by metabolomics. The blood-entering components were profiled by serum pharmacochemistry. The primary targets and signaling pathways of ECOTS were predicted through network pharmacology analysis. These predictions were further validated using immunohistochemical, immunofluorescence, and Western blot. RESULTS: ECOTS significantly suppressed inflammation and mitigated lung tissue damage in CS-induced mice. Network pharmacology screening and verification experiments revealed that the protective effects of ECOTS may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling in vivo and in vitro. Furthermore, the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P apparently impaired the effects of ECOTS in CS extract (CSE)-exposed BEAS-2B cells. CONCLUSION: ECOTS attenuates CS-induced COPD-like pathological changes in mice, and these protective effects may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling. This study extends previous evidence for the anti-COPD activity of the COTS and provides a potential mechanistic and pharmacological basis for its further investigation in COPD.

articles.title: Cicer arietinum seed extract attenuates doxorubicin-induced female reproductive toxicity in rats: Effects on oxidative stress, apoptosis-related markers, and PI3K/AKT-associated protein levels.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cicer arietinum is a nutritional and medicinal legume rich in bioactive phytochemicals with potential antioxidant and reproductive protective properties. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the protective effects of C. arietinum seed extract (CAE) against doxorubicin (DOX)-induced female reproductive toxicity in rats, focusing on oxidative stress, apoptosis-related markers, and PI3K/AKT signaling proteins. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The phytochemical profile of CAE was analyzed using LC-ESI-MS. Female Wistar rats were treated with DOX alone or in combination with CAE (250 or 500 mg/kg). Reproductive hormones, oxidative stress biomarkers, apoptosis-related gene expression, total PI3K and AKT protein levels, DNA damage, as well as histopathological and immunohistochemical changes were evaluated in both ovarian and uterine tissues. RESULTS: CAE ameliorated DOX-induced reproductive tissue injury, as demonstrated by improved hormonal profiles, reduced oxidative stress and DNA damage, and preservation of ovarian and uterine histoarchitecture. These improvements were accompanied by increased Bcl-2, Nrf2 and PARP-1expression, reduced Casp3, Bax, p53, CYP1A1, NF-κB and eNOS expression, and modulated total PI3K and AKT protein levels. CONCLUSION: CAE mitigated DOX-induced reproductive injury in female rats, potentially through modulation of oxidative stress, apoptosis-related molecular markers, and total PI3K and AKT protein levels. These findings suggest that CAE warrants further investigation as a potential protective agent against chemotherapy-associated reproductive toxicity.

articles.title: UHPLC-QTOF-MS profiling and antiplasmodial activity of extract and triterpenoids of Maytenus senegalensis: in vitro, in silico, and molecular dynamics studies.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Maytenus senegalensis (Lam.) Exell is widely used in traditional medicine across sub-Saharan Africa, including Cameroon, for the treatment of malaria. However, the specific bioactive compounds underlying its antiplasmodial properties remain poorly characterized. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the preliminary antiplasmodial activity of the trunk bark extracts and fractions of M. senegalensis and to characterize their chemical composition. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Trunk bark powder was macerated in dichloromethane/methanol (1:1, v/v) to obtain a crude extract, which was fractionated with n-hexane, ethyl acetate, and methanol. Fractions were tested against chloroquine-sensitive (PfNF54) and multidrug-resistant (PfDd2) strains of Plasmodium falciparum using the SYBR Green I fluorescence assay. The most active fraction was further purified by column chromatography. Phytochemical profiling of the crude extract and fractions was performed using UHPLC-QTOF-MS, and identified compounds were evaluated in silico for their binding affinities to malaria drug targets. RESULTS: The crude extract showed notable activity against PfDd2 (IC50 = 12.43 μg/mL). The ethyl acetate fraction was the most potent, with IC50 values of 3.48 μg/mL (PfDd2) and 7.96 μg/mL (PfNF54). UHPLC-QTOF-MS analysis revealed several triterpenes, among which maytenonic acid was isolated as a major constituent. Molecular docking indicated that 15α-hydroxy-21-keto-pristimerine and maytensifolone exhibited strong and consistent binding affinities toward PfNDH2, Plasmepsin II, and Falcipain-2. CONCLUSIONS: The antiplasmodial activity of M. senegalensis is largely attributable to its triterpene-rich ethyl acetate fraction. These findings provide a scientific rationale for its ethnomedicinal use in Cameroon and highlight its potential as a source of novel antimalarial leads against drug-resistant Plasmodium strains.

articles.title: Miao medicine Xinlikang capsule attenuates acute erythroleukemia through immune regulation and FLI1-PI3K axis-mediated cell cycle arrest.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Acute erythroleukemia (AEL) is an aggressive subtype of acute myeloid leukemia characterized by impaired erythroid differentiation, uncontrolled expansion of erythroid progenitors, and immune dysfunction. Owing to its poor prognosis and lack of specific therapeutic options, effective alternative strategies are urgently needed. Xinlikang capsules (XLK), a Miao medicine formula approved in China, have been clinically used as an adjuvant therapy for malignant tumors. However, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in AEL remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the anti-AEL effects of XLK and clarify its pharmacodynamic material basis and molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An AEL mouse model was established by F-MuLV infection and treated with XLK for 5 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed by serum biochemical indicators, organ indices, histopathological examination, immune cell profiling, erythroid differentiation markers, and survival analysis. The chemical compositions of XLK and XLK-containing serum (XLKs) were identified by UPLC-MS/MS. The anti-proliferative effects of XLKs and its absorbed constituents were evaluated in HEL cells using MTT assays and flow cytometry. Network pharmacology, RNA-seq, Western blotting, and Fli1 shRNA knockdown were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. This integrated approach evaluates in vivo therapeutic efficacy, defines the pharmacodynamic material basis, and dissects the molecular mechanism, providing a multi-layered analytical framework for understanding the anti-AEL effects of XLK. RESULTS: XLK markedly reduced splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, improved spleen and liver histopathological damage, normalized serum ALT and AST levels, and prolonged the survival of F-MuLV-induced AEL mice (p<0.001). XLK promoted erythroid maturation by increasing mature erythroid cells and reducing erythroid precursor accumulation. It also restored immune homeostasis, as evidenced by increased CD3+ T cells (by 50%), CD11b+ cells (by 10%), and B220+ B cells (by 46%), together with a normalized CD4+/CD8a+ ratio in the spleen. UPLC-MS/MS identified nine absorbed constituents in XLKs, among which tomentic acid, tanshinone IIA, cryptotanshinone, and apigenin exhibited notable inhibitory effects on HEL cell proliferation. XLKs suppressed HEL cell proliferation (27.69% inhibition at 72 h with 20% XLKs) and induced S-phase arrest in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. Network pharmacology and RNA-seq analyses indicated that the PI3K signaling pathway and cell cycle regulation were key pathways involved in the anti-AEL effects of XLK. Mechanistically, XLKs downregulated FLI1 and inhibited PI3K pathway activation in HEL cells, accompanied by decreased CDK2 and Cyclin B1 expression and increased Cyclin A2 (1.9-fold) and p-CDC25C (1.7-fold) expression. Furthermore, Fli1 knockdown reduced p-PI3K and attenuated the anti-proliferative effect of XLKs (8.51% reduction at 72 h), supporting a key role of FLI1-mediated PI3K signaling in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest. Among the absorbed constituents, cryptotanshinone recapitulated the downregulation of FLI1, p-PI3K, and p-mTOR, supporting its role in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that XLK exerts therapeutic effects in F-MuLV-induced AEL. Mechanistically, XLK alleviated spleen and liver injury, promoted erythroid differentiation, restored immune homeostasis, and suppressed erythroleukemia cell proliferation by inducing cell-cycle arrest through modulation of the FLI1-PI3K signaling pathway, thereby exerting a therapeutic effect on AEL.

articles.title: Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) alleviates inflammation-driven perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 cascade.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction is closely correlated with chronic ovarian inflammation and decreased ovarian reserve, with the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory pathway serving as the core pathogenic regulator. Targeted inhibition of this inflammatory signaling cascade and subsequent ovarian cell apoptosis is a key therapeutic approach for improving perimenopausal ovarian lesions. Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT), a classic TCM formula, clears internal heat and nourishes yin and blood, and is traditionally used for perimenopausal night sweats due to yin deficiency with internal heat. Consistent with the pathology of perimenopausal ovarian inflammatory injury, these traditional properties provide an ethnopharmacological basis for alleviating chronic ovarian inflammation and protecting granulosa cells, supporting its potential in treating perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) and its heat-clearing herb group (QRJD) on ovarian dysfunction in a natural perimenopause (PM) rat model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHPLC-MS/MS characterized the chemical and blood-absorbed components of DGLHT and QRJD. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified core targets and bioactive constituents. Naturally aged rats (12-14 months old) were randomized into Control, PM, DGLH-L/M/H, QRJD, and celecoxib (CEL) groups. Parameters assessed included body weight, ovarian index, estrous cyclicity, serum sex hormones, follicular atresia, granulosa cell apoptosis, inflammatory factors in serum and ovarian tissue, and the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway activity. Validation was performed in TLR4-overexpressing KGN cells treated with DGLHT-containing serum. RESULTS: Baicalein and Wogonin were identified as key blood-absorbed components targeting TLR4, Caspase-3, IL-1β, and TNF-α. Both DGLHT and QRJD restored estrous cycles, improved ovarian coefficients, expanded the pool of healthy follicles, and reduced follicular atresia rates. Additionally, both formulations reduced granulosa cell apoptosis, corrected hormonal imbalances (increased E2 and P4, decreased FSH and LH), and downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-18, TNF-α) and key proteins (TLR4, NF-κB p65, NLRP3, Caspase-3). Their anti-inflammatory efficacy was comparable to that of CEL, with medium- and high-dose DGLHT demonstrating superior endocrine protection. In vitro, DGLHT-containing serum inhibited TLR4-overexpression-induced activation of the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis. CONCLUSIONS: DGLHT and QRJD alleviate chronic ovarian inflammation, inhibit granulosa cell apoptosis, reduce follicular atresia, and correct sex hormone imbalances by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway. Consequently, they improve ovarian reserve function in the rat model of PM and alleviate PM-associated ovarian dysfunction.

articles.title: L-asparagine alleviates osteoarthritis via inhibiting chondrocyte ferroptosis through the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic degenerative joint disease, with amino acid metabolic dysregulation and chondrocyte ferroptosis implicated in its pathogenesis. This study aims to investigate the chondroprotective effects of L-asparagine (Asn) and elucidate its molecular mechanisms in targeting ferroptosis. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was employed to assess the causal relationship between plasma Asn levels and OA risk, while network pharmacology and transcriptomics were integrated to identify core targets and pathways. The regulatory effects of Asn on ferroptosis and extracellular matrix homeostasis were systematically evaluated in IL-1β-stimulated ATDC5 chondrocytes and a destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) mouse model of OA, with Nutlin-3 rescue experiments confirming the involvement of the p53/solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11)/glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) axis. Elevated plasma Asn was causally linked to reduced OA risk. In vitro, Asn attenuated IL-1β-induced chondrocyte damage, curtailed reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and lipid peroxidation, and restored mitochondrial ultrastructural integrity, concomitant with upregulated SLC7A11, GPX4, and type II collagen (COL2), alongside downregulated p53, ACSL4, and MMP13-effects that were partially reversed by Nutlin-3 co-administration. In vivo, Asn ameliorated cartilage degeneration and subchondral bone erosion in DMM mice. Collectively, Asn suppresses chondrocyte ferroptosis through the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 axis, retarding OA progression. These findings provide novel mechanistic evidence and identify a potential therapeutic candidate for the management of OA.

articles.title: HDAC6 Inhibition Promotes Peripheral Nerve Development and Regeneration via Neurofilament Acetylation.
articles.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to limited neuronal regeneration. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) regulates microtubule dynamics, but its role in peripheral nervous system (PNS) development and repair is incompletely understood. This study investigates the expression, function, and mechanism of HDAC6 in PNS maturation and regeneration. HDAC6 was abundantly expressed in dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerves. During postnatal development (P1-P28), HDAC6 expression progressively declined, inversely correlating with increased α-tubulin K40 and global acetylation. Pharmacological HDAC6 inhibition with Tubastatin A (Tub A) or suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) accelerated nerve maturation, evidenced by enhanced conduction velocity, myelination, and cytoskeletal integrity. In a sciatic nerve crush model, HDAC6 inhibition promoted functional recovery, axonal regeneration, and remyelination. In vitro, HDAC6 inhibition or siRNA knockdown enhanced neurite outgrowth and growth cone expansion in both motor and sensory neurons. Mechanistically, acetylome identified neurofilament light chain (NEFL) as a novel HDAC6 substrate. Among several hypoacetylated lysine residues post-injury, K316 showed the greatest decrease. Direct HDAC6-NEFL interaction was confirmed by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation. Expression of an acetylation-mimetic NEFL (K316Q) mutant promoted neurite outgrowth and growth cone maturation compared with wild-type or acetylation-deficient (K316R) mutants. Collectively, HDAC6 acts as a key negative regulator of PNS development and regeneration, and NEFL K316 acetylation serves as a critical molecular switch for axonal growth. Targeting HDAC6 represents a promising strategy for peripheral nerve repair.

articles.title: Targeting FSP1 to Suppress PI3K/AKT Signaling: Enarodustat Ameliorates MASH via Ferroptosis Inhibition and Lipid Metabolism Regulation.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a serious global public health problem with limited effective therapies. Previous studies have shown that ferroptosis and abnormal PI3K/AKT signaling play critical roles in its pathogenesis. Enarodustat, a hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor for anemia, inhibitor approved for anemia, whose therapeutic effects and mechanisms in MASH remain unexplored. This study investigated enarodustat's effects and molecular mechanisms in FFA-induced HepG2/AML12 hepatocytes and CDAHFD-induced MASH mice. Enarodustat dose-dependently reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, triglyceride and cholesterol levels, alleviated steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, liver injury and oxidative stress. Mechanistically, it bound to and upregulated FSP1, inhibiting ferroptosis and lipid peroxidation; it also suppressed overactivated PI3K/AKT pathway, regulated the SIRT1/PPARα/SREBP-1c axis, reducing lipogenesis, enhancing fatty acid oxidation and downregulating inflammation- and fibrosis-related genes. FSP1 knockdown and PI3K/AKT inhibition confirmed its protective effects rely on FSP1-mediated ferroptosis inhibition and PI3K/AKT regulation. This study first demonstrates enarodustat has significant therapeutic potential for MASH by targeting FSP1 to coordinately ameliorate lipid metabolism disorders and ferroptosis, providing a novel strategy and candidate drug.

articles.title: Functional contribution of TERT to mitigation of endometrial stromal cell senescence by metformin through modulation of the AKT/mTOR axis.
articles.abstract: Uterine aging contributes significantly to infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in women of advanced reproductive age. While telomere dysfunction and cellular senescence are established hallmarks of aging, therapeutic strategies targeting these processes in the uterus remain limited. This study investigated the effects of metformin on senescence-associated phenotypes in hTERT-immortalized human endometrial stromal cells (THESCs) and examined the potential contribution of TERT and AKT/mTOR signaling. Through an integrative network pharmacology approach, we identified 37 overlapping targets related to metformin, senescence, and uterine function, with TERT, AKT, and mTOR emerging as key targets. Metformin significantly restored cell proliferation, reduced senescence markers (P16, P21), and alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress in late-passage and D-galactose-treated THESCs. Notably, Metformin also increased relative telomere length and TERT expression. TERT knockdown attenuated selected metformin-associated effects, including changes in cellular phenotypes and AKT/mTOR signaling, supporting a functional contribution of TERT. Exploratory molecular docking identified predicted binding poses of metformin with TERT, AKT, and mTOR. Moreover, metformin treatment in aged mice was associated with improved uterine histological features and changes in TERT, AKT, mTOR, and P16 immunoreactivity, and an increased number of pups. Collectively, these findings support a functional contribution of TERT to selected metformin-associated responses in THESCs, accompanied by changes in mitochondrial and redox phenotypes and AKT/mTOR phosphorylation. Further studies are required to define the causal relationships among these pathways and determine their relevance to physiological reproductive aging.

articles.title: Optimization and in vitro evaluation of hydroxychloroquine loaded melanin-like polydopamine nanoparticles as a biomimetic drug delivery system against B16F10 melanoma cells.
articles.abstract: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) has shown anticancer potential mainly through autophagy inhibition; however, insufficient cellular delivery and nonspecific distribution limit its efficacy as a standalone therapy. This study aimed to develop HCQ-loaded melanin-like polydopamine nanoparticles (HCQ-PDA NPs) and PEGylated derivatives (HCQ-mPEG-PDA NPs) as biomimetic nanocarriers to enhance HCQ activity against melanoma cells. PDA NPs were prepared by spontaneous oxidative polymerization, and critical formulation variables were optimized using a Box-Behnken design. The optimized PDA-based NPs displayed suitable nanoscale characteristics, with particle sizes of 131.93-159.73 nm, low polydispersity indices of 0.184-0.209, and negative zeta potentials ranging from -42.17 to -28.37 mV. HCQ-loaded formulations showed encapsulation efficiencies of 45.83-47.93% and HCQ incorporation relative to initial dopamine of 9.17-9.59%. PDA NPs exhibited significantly faster initial HCQ release at pH 6.0 than at pH 7.4 during the first 2 h, whereas the release profiles converged at later time points and reached approximately 86% cumulative release within 24 h. In B16F10 melanoma cells, both HCQ-PDA NPs and HCQ-mPEG-PDA NPs exhibited in vitro cytotoxic activity. Compared with free HCQ, HCQ-mPEG-PDA NPs significantly reduced cell viability at 24, 48, and 72 h, whereas HCQ-PDA NPs showed a significant reduction only at 48 h. In addition, clonogenic and wound-healing assays confirmed suppression of colony formation and reduced wound closure following PDA NPs treatment. Ultimately, HCQ incorporation into PEGylated PDA nanoplatforms can significantly improve its standalone anticancer performance against melanoma cells, offering a promising approach for further investigation in melanoma therapy.

articles.title: Molecular insights into the interactions of green-synthesized γ-Fe2O3@SiO2-penciclovir nanoparticles with human serum albumin and lysozyme: A multi-spectroscopic and molecular docking study.
articles.abstract: The formation of a protein corona at the nano-bio interface critically governs the biological identity, circulation, and therapeutic performance of nanoparticle (NP)-based drug delivery systems. However, the molecular basis of the interactions between drug-loaded magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) and plasma proteins remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the molecular interactions of green-synthesized γ-Fe2O3@SiO2-penciclovir (PNV) MNPs with human serum albumin (HSA) and lysozyme (Lys) under physiological conditions using UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, and molecular docking analyses. UV-Vis spectroscopy suggested the formation of ground-state complexes, while fluorescence quenching revealed moderate binding affinity and suggested approximately one dominant binding site per protein molecule. Thermodynamic analyses suggested that hydrophobic interactions may contribute to HSA binding, whereas hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces may contribute to Lys binding. Negative Gibbs free energy values indicated that both binding processes were thermodynamically favorable under the investigated conditions. CD spectroscopy revealed slight decreases in ellipticity without appreciable shifts in the characteristic bands of HSA and Lys upon interaction with the MNPs. Molecular docking identified the key amino acid residues potentially involved in NP-protein binding, providing additional molecular-level insights into the interactions observed spectroscopically. Collectively, these findings advance our molecular understanding of NP-protein interactions relevant to protein corona formation and provide a basis for further research into the development of safer, more stable, and biologically compatible magnetic nanocarriers for targeted drug delivery.

articles.title: Hydrogel crosslinking mechanisms influence the release and functional delivery of lipid nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Hydrogels have emerged as attractive vaccine delivery platforms because they enable controlled modulation of antigen availability. However, how different hydrogel environments affect the release and functionality of mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the release, stability, cellular uptake, and transfection capability of LNPs released from four hydrogel systems representing distinct crosslinking mechanisms: covalently crosslinked poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), ionically crosslinked alginate, thermoresponsive Poloxamer 407 (P407), and protein-based Matrigel/collagen hydrogels. All hydrogel types enabled release of LNPs over days, with lower polymer concentrations generally exhibiting faster nanoparticle release. PEG offered greatest tunability of release kinetics; at the same time the recovery of the LNP-incorporated fluorescent dye DiI was reduced to about 80 %, indicating partial dye leakage. Alginate hydrogels exhibited recovery of DiI below 50 % and broader particle size distributions after release, while P407 hydrogels largely preserved LNP characteristics. CyroTEM analysis revealed that mRNA-LNPs kept at 37°C, including those released from hydrogels, exhibited a more compact and electron-dense morphology than mRNA-LNPs maintained at 4°C. Notably, although quantitative recovery from Matrigel/collagen hydrogels was limited, released LNPs achieved approximately 80-90 % of the eGFP expression compared to mRNA-LNPs that have not been embedded. Importantly, cellular uptake and transfection experiments demonstrated that all investigated hydrogels released biologically active mRNA-LNPs capable of mediating protein expression. Moreover, our findings show that hydrogel composition is a critical determinant of mRNA-LNP release, stability, functional delivery and morphology of the released particles. This work provides design principles for the development of hydrogel-based mRNA delivery systems aimed at sustained antigen availability and prolonged vaccine responses.

articles.title: Sustained delivery of TNF-α inhibitors using HAP/PDA-functionalized porous PLGA-based microspheres for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
articles.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors (TNFi) are a cornerstone of biological therapy for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet their clinical efficacy is often compromised by rapid systemic clearance and frequent administration, while preservation of protein bioactivity remains a major challenge for long-acting delivery systems. Here, we report HAP/PDA-functionalized porous poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)-based microspheres for sustained delivery of TNFi. By integrating hydroxyapatite (HAP)-mediated buffering of the degradation microenvironment with polydopamine (PDA)-enabled interfacial regulation, the composite microspheres enable high protein loading, reduced burst release, and sustained delivery of biologically active TNFi. HAP mitigates degradation-associated acidification, whereas PDA enhances protein retention and regulates release through interfacial interactions. In vitro, TNFi released from the functionalized microspheres retained anti-inflammatory activity, suppressing TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β secretion by M1-polarized macrophages and attenuating inflammation-induced proliferation and migration of rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes. In a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model, the TNFi-loaded microspheres prolonged apparent systemic TNFi exposure following subcutaneous administration, reduced arthritis severity and joint swelling, and protected against synovial inflammation and cartilage destruction compared with free TNFi, without overt histopathological abnormalities in major organs. These findings support HAP/PDA-functionalized porous PLGA-based microspheres as a long-acting subcutaneous TNFi formulation and illustrate the value of jointly regulating the PLGA degradation microenvironment and the protein-carrier interface.

articles.title: Hydrophobic ion pairing enabled self-nanoemulsifying niclosamide for pancreatic cancer: improved drug loading and kinetic solubility.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive and relatively uncommon disease characterized by profound dense fibrosis and late-stage diagnosis. An anthelmintic drug, Niclosamide (NIC), has been widely repurposed as an anticancer agent, but its poor aqueous solubility resulted in < 10 % oral bioavailability, while its poor lipid solubility poses substantial challenges for the development of a translational oral formulation. Herein, we have developed a self-nanoemulsifying (SNEDDS) formulation (NanoNic) that utilizes Transcutol® P as cosolvent and leverages the Hydrophobic Ion-Pairing (HIP) complexation strategy to improve drug loading and stability. To this end, we screened cationic complexing agents with different amine functionalities - primary, ternary and quaternary. Cationic ionizable lipid/DLin-DMA was selected as pairing agent based on its superior biocompatibility, complexation efficiency, and kinetic stability. Incorporation of cationic ionizable lipid forming a hydrophobic complex with NIC resulted in nearly 30 % reduction in globule size to ∼ 67 nm with a zeta potential >+35 mV. Optimized NanoNic (HIP-loaded SNEDDS) demonstrated ∼ 4-fold higher drug-loading compared to traditional SNEDDS (without a complexing agent), which showed immediate drug precipitation after redispersion. HIP-loaded NanoNic preconcentrate was stable for over 3 months, whereas its aqueous dispersion exhibited only 2 % drug precipitation within 24 h. The Quality-by-Design approach was employed to optimize the nano-globule size of the formulation/NanoNic. Furthermore, NanoNic displayed significant anti-angiogenic activity (HUVEC model) and anticancer efficacy in 2D and 3D models of naïve and gemcitabine-resistant MiaPaCa-2 spheroids. Thus, collective use of Transcutol®P and Ionizable lipid enabled self-nanoemulsifying system with high drug load, reduced globule size and high kinetic solubility.

articles.title: Inter-laboratory validation study of an in vitro retinoic acid receptor transactivation assay for testing potential endocrine disrupting chemicals.
articles.abstract: The retinoic acid receptors belong to the family of nuclear receptor transcription factors. These receptors regulate various physiological processes, such as neurodevelopment, growth, cellular metabolism, and reproduction. Disruption of retinoic acid receptor activity by environmental chemicals can potentially have detrimental effects and warrant the design and validation of methods to identify such compounds. Here we report the results from a ring-trial validation study of a cell-based RAR transactivation assay involving four laboratories. The laboratories set up the assay and tested 30 selected chemicals, with good concordance. There was agreement between all laboratories for the classification of activity in 80% of the cases, and three or more laboratories were in agreement for 93%. The combined results were also in agreement with the expected outcome for the selected chemicals in 90% of the cases. The assay was, thus, deemed easily transferable and reproducible between laboratories, since they arrived at the same qualitative results. Overall, the transfer and validation were successful, and the method is under evaluation to become an Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development test guideline for detection of endocrine disrupting chemicals. The method is expected to become valuable for hazard identification together with other similar methods, for assessing chemicals or environmental samples.

articles.title: Glyoxalase - 1 inhibition reduces endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor-mediated relaxation of the rat superior mesenteric artery.
articles.abstract: EDHF-type relaxation is frequently impaired in diabetes-related diseases, possibly due to glycative toxicity. GLO1 detoxifies methylglyoxal and suppresses accumulation of AGEs, so the current study examined the potential contribution of reduced GLO1 activity to endogenous glycative stress and vascular impairment. We examined the effects of the GLO1 inhibitor BBGC on arterial relaxation, with particular emphasis on EDHF-type relaxations. The isolated rat superior mesenteric arterial rings were cultured for 24 h in high-glucose medium (approximately 25 mmol/L) with vehicle or BBGC (10-5 mol/L). No statistically significant differences were detected in overall ACh-induced relaxation or in response to SNP and cromakalim. However, BBGC markedly reduced ACh-induced EDHF-type relaxation compared to vehicle treatment. Combined SKCa and IKCa blockade virtually abolished the residual relaxation in both groups, and no between-group difference was detected during KCa-channel blockade. Aminoguanidine co-treatment increased ACh-induced EDHF-type relaxation in BBGC-treated arteries. These results suggest that BBGC attenuated EDHF-type relaxation under high-glucose culture conditions. The findings are consistent with a possible contribution of GLO1 to KCa-dependent relaxation, although the roles of MGO accumulation and channel dysfunction remain unconfirmed.

articles.title: The molecule-independent device bridging approach (MIDBA): perspective on advancing the evidence base for platform-informed bridging.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The need for drug delivery solutions supporting launch of subcutaneously administered biotherapeutics in decentralized care settings has increased interest in abbreviated but scientifically justified clinical device bridging strategies. The recently adopted Qualification Opinion by the CHMP on the Molecule-Independent Device Bridging Approach (MIDBA) established a regulatory framework for clinical bridging from manual injection to an autoinjector for monoclonal antibodies. While the Qualification Opinion applies solely to the regulatory context of the European Medicines Agency and does pertain to other regulatory authorities outside the European Union, it represents an important milestone in the evolution of clinical device bridging. AREAS COVERED: This Expert Opinion examines MIDBA's underlying scientific principles to guide data generation beyond the qualified context of use. The author distinguishes the CHMP-qualified MIDBA from a broader, author-proposed platform-informed device bridging framework, also discussing considerations for large-volume automated injection devices and additional therapeutic modalities. EXPERT OPINION: A basic decision matrix is proposed to identify device bridging scenarios where existing platform evidence may be leveraged. Categorizing molecules based on absorption profile susceptibility to administration conditions and early/peak concentration clinical relevance, this matrix is expected to provide a basis for evaluating future bridging and associated platform data generation while recognizing evidence requirements remain context specific.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates cognitive impairment after traumatic brain injury with involvement of NMDAR-related signaling.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) can cause persistent cognitive impairment accompanied by neuronal and synaptic damage. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) has neuroprotective properties, but the signaling processes associated with its effects after TBI remain incompletely understood. Adult male mice underwent controlled cortical impact and received intraperitoneal AS-IV during a 28-day post-injury period, with GM1 included as a positive control. Behavioral assessments, immunofluorescence, Golgi-Cox staining, transmission electron microscopy, and immunoblotting were combined with NMDAR antagonist co-treatment and exploratory docking, molecular dynamics, and cellular thermal shift analyses. AS-IV treatment improved cognitive performance and was associated with preservation of dendritic and synaptic structure, increased NMDAR subunit expression, and changes in ERK1/2, CaMKII, and CREB phosphorylation and synapse-associated proteins. The 40 mg/kg dose showed greater effects than 80 mg/kg for several outcomes. Co-treatment with MK-801 or TCN-201 attenuated multiple AS-IV-associated effects, supporting involvement of NMDAR-related signaling. Computational predictions and NMDAR2A thermal stabilization were consistent with possible receptor engagement but did not establish direct binding, binding affinity, or receptor activation. Collectively, these findings suggest that modulation of NMDAR-related signaling alterations may contribute to the cognitive and synaptic structural and molecular effects associated with AS-IV after TBI. However, the present data do not establish direct NMDAR binding or activation, in vivo target occupancy, or NMDAR as the exclusive or primary molecular target of AS-IV.

articles.title: Integrated chemical profiling and lipidomics reveal that Mailuoning oral liquid alleviates diet-induced MASLD via PPARα-mediated lipid homeostasis and COX-2 inhibition, with identification of potential active constituents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mailuoning oral liquid (MLN), a standardized five-herb formula, is used for ischemic vascular diseases and shows potential in ameliorating dyslipidemia. Our previous study showed MLN alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) via peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) activation, but its comprehensive chemical profile, systemic exposure, and bioactive constituents mediating both PPARα activation and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibition remain unclear. METHODS: High-fat, high-fructose diet-fed rats received MLN (5.4 or 10.8 mL/kg/day) for 8 weeks. Ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with Q-Exactive Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap HRMS) profiled MLN chemicals and identified serum/liver prototypes. Biochemical profiles, glucose tolerance, histopathology, untargeted lipidomics, and targeted polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) analysis were performed. PPARα and COX-2 signaling were examined by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Key constituents were screened for PPARα activation via dual luciferase reporter assay and molecular docking; COX-2 inhibition was validated by enzyme assays and molecular dynamics. RESULTS: A total of 143 compounds were characterized; 48 and 92 prototypes were enriched in serum and liver, respectively. MLN ameliorated dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, steatosis, and inflammation. Lipidomics revealed bidirectional modulation of hepatic lipids, reversing triglyceride (TAG) accumulation and restoring phosphatidylcholine (PC) and lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) levels. Targeted analysis showed increased eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and normalized COX-2-derived prostaglandins (PGD2, PGE2). MLN activated hepatic PPARα and downregulated COX-2. Seven serum-enriched compounds (chlorogenic acid, macranthoidin B, luteoloside, harpagide, angoroside C, oleanolic acid, betaine) were validated as direct PPARα agonists. Secologanoside and chikusetsusaponin IVa were identified as novel COX-2 inhibitors (half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) = 14.61 and 120.9 nM). DISCUSSION: MLN alleviates MASLD via dual PPARα activation and COX-2 inhibition, providing a mechanistic foundation for repurposing this herbal formula in early-stage MASLD.

articles.title: Integrating tissue proteomics and bioactive lipid analysis of ovine tissue samples identifies functional relations of bioactive lipids.
articles.abstract: Bioactive lipids are potent effector molecules that may help to reveal specific information about biological processes. However, analytical challenges and incomplete functional annotations remain as obstacles. We hypothesized that the functional annotation of these lipids may be improved by projecting enriched Gene Ontology (GO) terms derived from proteomics to correlating bioactive lipids. To that aim, thirteen organs and tissues from sheep (Ovis aries) were analyzed using mass spectrometry-based untargeted proteomics and bioactive lipid analysis. In total, 4717 proteins and 168 bioactive lipids, including fatty acids and their conjugates, oxylipins (octadecanoids, eicosanoids, and docosanoids), lyso-phosphatidylcholines (LPCs) and lyso-phosphatidylethanolamines (LPEs), endocannabinoids and related fatty amides, and bile acids and related sterol lipids were determined. Thereof, the correct identification of 114 lipids was confirmed using commercially available analytical standards, whereas the identity of the previously uncharacterized oxylipin 4-hydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (4-HETE) was verified through in-house chemical synthesis. Co-expression and clustering analyses are consistent with our hypothesis via independently corroborating known bioactive lipid functions and suggested novel functional relations. Amongst other observations, 18-HETE and 19-HETE were related to mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, 11,12-dihydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (DiHETE), 15-deoxy-prostaglandin J2 and 5(6)-epoxy-eicosatrienoic acid (EET) were related to chemical synaptic transmission, arachidonoyl ethanolamide phosphate was related to muscle contraction and numerous LPCs and LPEs were related to exosome formation. Tissue levels of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), pro-resolving mediators and the newly characterized 4-HETE were related to the cellular protein synthesis and folding machinery. The latter finding suggested that PUFAs and their derivatives support protein synthesis fidelity in addition to efferocytosis, both essential contributors for the effective resolution of inflammation.

articles.title: Association between statin therapy and dementia risk: evidence from All of Us and UK Biobank with coenzyme Q7-related mediation analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Statins are widely prescribed for cardiovascular disease prevention in older adults; however, their association with dementia remains controversial. Given the high prevalence of both statin use and cognitive decline in aging populations, clarifying this relationship has critical implications for geriatric clinical practice and shared decision-making. METHODS: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study using the All of Us Research Program (discovery cohort, n = 83,355; 31,513 statin users) and UK Biobank (replication cohort, n = 173,282; 43,976 statin users). Participants were adults aged ≥40 years who self-identified as White, followed from 2006 through 2023 (discovery) and 2017 (replication). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline characteristics. Dementia risk was estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. An exploratory mediation analysis examined low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and coenzyme Q7, a protein involved in CoQ10 biosynthesis, as potential pathways linking statin use and dementia. RESULTS: Statin use was associated with significantly increased dementia risk in both cohorts (discovery: adjusted HR 2.22, 95% CI 2.02-2.44; replication: adjusted HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.98-3.33). Clear intensity-dependent relationships were observed, with high-intensity statins conferring 14% greater risk than moderate-to-low intensity therapy. In the exploratory mediation analysis, the estimated indirect effect through coenzyme Q7 was statistically significant and accounted for 8.2% of the total association, whereas the indirect effect through LDL-C was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: Statin use was associated with higher dementia risk in both cohorts, and exploratory mediation findings suggested a modest statistical indirect association through COQ7, which should be considered hypothesis-generating. Given the observational design and conflicting evidence in the literature, these findings warrant further investigation before informing clinical decisions about statin therapy.

articles.title: Epimedium koreanum Nakai attenuates glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by suppressing ferroptosis via the KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 axis: comparative pharmacodynamic evaluation of four epimedium species and proteomic and metabolomic analyses of epk.
articles.abstract: Objective: The pharmacodynamics and underlying mechanisms of Epimedium (Yingyanghuo), a traditional Chinese medicine, were investigated in the context of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) management, with particular emphasis on ferroptosis inhibition.Methods: A rat model of GIOP was developed through dexamethasone (DEX) administration. Animals received extracts of the four Epimedium species; Epimedium koreanum Nakai (Epk) was selected for subsequent investigation owing to its superior preliminary efficacy. Evaluations encompassed bone microstructure, osteoclast activity, serum biomarkers of bone metabolism, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation and iron accumulation indicators (4-HNE and Fe2+), and ferroptosis-associated proteins (KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway). Integration of proteomics and metabolomics facilitated the identification of key pathways, followed by experimental validation of ferroptosis modulation.Results: Epk treatment mitigated DEX-induced bone loss, improved bone microarchitecture, and suppressed osteoclast activity. Multi-omics approaches uncovered reversal of 368 proteins and 127 metabolites in GIOP rats following Epk administration, with enrichment observed in ferroptosis, glutathione metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation. Treatment with Epk further reduced the elevated femoral 4-HNE and Fe2+ levels in GIOP rats. Epk treatment elevated NRF2, HO-1, SLC7A11, and GPX4 and reduced KEAP1 and P53 in bone tissue, consistent with suppression of ferroptosis-related signaling.Conclusion: Epimedium, with Epk as the prominent representative, confers substantial protection against GIOP, with effects associated with modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway and suppression of ferroptosis-related markers in bone tissue, thereby providing a basis for further investigation of its clinical potential in GIOP management.

articles.title: Ambrisentan ameliorates methotrexate nephrotoxicity through modulation of RhoA/ROCK and PI3K/MDM2-associated signaling: network pharmacology-guided discovery and in vivo confirmation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Methotrexate (MTX) is a potent antineoplastic agent; however, its clinical application is frequently limited by nephrotoxicity, which may result in treatment interruption. Previous evidence indicates that MTX can promote endothelin-1 (ET-1)-associated renal injury. Therefore, this study investigated whether blocking ET-1 receptors with Ambrisentan (AMB) could alleviate MTX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). METHODS: Network pharmacology analysis was performed to identify potential targets and pathways associated with AMB and MTX-induced AKI. For In-vivo validation, twenty-four rats were divided into four groups: control, AMB, MTX, and MTX+AMB. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Network pharmacology identified 102 overlapping targets between AMB and MTX-induced AKI, with 20 hub genes identified through protein-protein interaction network analysis, highlighting PPAR-γ as a key target. KEGG pathway enrichment revealed the involvement of RhoA/ROCK and PI3K-associated signaling pathways, in correlation with inflammatory and apoptotic markers. Experimentally, AMB co-treatment improved renal function parameters and histopathological alterations, restored oxidative balance, and attenuated MTX-induced inflammatory and apoptotic responses, including ICAM-1, NF-κB, RhoA/ROCK, Bax, Caspase-3 and p53. Furthermore, AMB restored the expression of PPAR-γ, PI3K, MDM2, and Bcl-2, suggesting the involvement of PI3K/MDM2-associated signaling alterations in AMB-mediated nephroprotection. In conclusion, AMB may mitigate MTX-induced nephrotoxicity through modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Further studies are required to evaluate its effects on MTX pharmacokinetics, renal elimination, antineoplastic efficacy, and therapeutic potential in established MTX-induced AKI.

articles.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation versus sham stimulation and dexamethasone versus amisulpride for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic gynecologic surgery: protocol for a randomized 2 × 2 factorial trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Although multimodal prophylaxis is recommended, clinical practice still relies largely on pharmacologic interventions. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) at the P6 acupoint may have potential benefit for PONV prevention. However, its effectiveness when incorporated into pharmacologic prophylaxis, and whether its effect varies according to the antiemetic used, remain unclear. This trial aims to evaluate the effect of P6-TEAS on PONV prevention in patients receiving dexamethasone or amisulpride. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial will enroll 212 women undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive one of four treatment combinations: TEAS plus dexamethasone, TEAS plus amisulpride, sham stimulation plus dexamethasone, or sham stimulation plus amisulpride. TEAS or sham stimulation will be delivered at the P6 acupoint in two 1-h sessions, before surgery and at 24 h after surgery. The primary outcome will be the incidence of PONV within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include PONV-related symptoms and severity, use of rescue antiemetics, opioid consumption, pain scores, recovery milestones, patient satisfaction, QoR-15 scores, and length of hospital stay. Safety outcomes will include adverse events related to TEAS or study drugs and perioperative hemodynamic events requiring treatment. DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate P6-TEAS versus sham stimulation as the primary comparison and provide exploratory estimates for the dexamethasone-versus-amisulpride comparison and the TEAS-by-drug interaction. The findings may inform integrated prevention strategies for PONV after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07631910, identifier NCT07631910.

articles.title: Multi-target effects of bergapten in a vitro periodontitis-mimicking model: suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress while promoting osteogenesis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bergapten (BG) is a natural furanocoumarin found in various botanical drugs including Citrus bergamia, Angelica archangelica, and Citrus medica, and it's a bioactive constituent of Peucedanum guangxiense, an indigenous species in Guangxi, China. Although BG exhibits anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective properties, its effects relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment remains unexplored. METHODS: This study integrated network analysis with in vitro experimental validation to investigate the multi-target effects of BG in a Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide (P.g-LPS) -induced periodontitis-mimicking in vitro model. RESULTS: Network analysis and molecular docking identified the PI3K/Akt pathway as a candidate pathway, along with predicted binding to CAT, BMP-2, TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β. BG at concentration of 5-30 μM did not reduce cell viability in human periodontal ligament stem cells (h-PDLSCs) or RAW264 .7 macrophages under the tested conditions. BG at concentrations of 7.5-30 μM directly promoted osteogenic differentiation of h-PDLSCs beyond baseline levels in the normal-mimicking microenvironment, as evidenced by increased ALP activity, mineralization, and expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2, COL-I, OCN, and OPN). Under inflammatory conditions, BG reduced intracellular oxidative activity across concentrations of 7.5-30 μM, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), down-regulated M1 macrophages polarization associated markers (iNOS, CD86) and NF-κB components (IκBα, p65), while up-regulating anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-4, IL-10), M2 macrophages polarization-associated markers (Arg-1, CD206) and antioxidant genes (HO-1,CAT, SOD). Moreover, BG-treated macrophages conditioned medium partially rescued the osteogenic capacity of h-PDLSCs in inflammation condition, though not to the level of the normal control. The effects might associate with increased phosphorylation levels of PI3K and Akt, and with decreased mRNA expression of NF-κB pathway components. CONCLUSION: Collectively, BG was associated with multi-modal effects relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, including alleviating oxidative stress, suppressing NF-κB driven inflammation, promoting PI3K/Akt associated osteogenesis, and shifting macrophage polarization-associated markers toward an M2-like profile. Our in vitro findings suggest that BG possess multi-modal activities relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, warranting further in vivo investigation to assess its pharmacological relevance.

articles.title: Multi-omics identifies PCK1-associated immunometabolic regulation underlying the protective effects of sinomenine in vascular dementia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular dementia (VaD) is one of the major causes of cognitive impairment among older adults. However, effective treatments that can modify the progression of the disease are still lacking. Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic remodeling in microglia influences inflammatory responses during vascular brain injury. Microglial immunometabolic regulation has therefore been proposed as an important contributor to the pathogenesis of vascular dementia (VaD). METHODS: Transcriptomic integration, WGCNA, network pharmacology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing were combined to identify disease-associated microglial alterations and potential targets involved in sinomenine (SIN)-mediated regulation. The interaction between SIN and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1) was investigated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. The biological effects of SIN were then validated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglia. RESULTS: Integrated analyses highlighted PCK1 as a potential mediator associated with SIN-induced metabolic regulation in VaD. snRNA-seq demonstrated expansion of metabolically stressed microglial states accompanied by PCK1-related metabolic alterations. Stable binding between SIN and PCK1 was supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia, SIN suppressed inflammatory activation, restored PCK1 expression, attenuated inflammation-associated metabolic remodeling, improved cellular bioenergetics, and modulated metabolic redox-related parameters. SIN also enhanced adaptive stress responses through regulation of CRYAB, APOD, and HSPH1. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings suggest that SIN alleviates VaD-associated microglial dysfunction by modulating PCK1-associated immunometabolic alterations. They expand the current understanding of the pharmacological actions of SIN and highlight microglial immunometabolic regulation as a potential therapeutic target for VaD.

articles.title: Berbamine exerts anti-breast-cancer effects in association with autophagy-related responses and PI3K/Akt1/mTOR signaling.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and effective, well-tolerated therapeutic strategies are needed. Berbamine (BBM), a natural bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid, has anticancer activity, but its effects on autophagy- and lysosome-related processes in breast cancer remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We evaluated the effects of BBM on MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, MCF-7, and 4T1 breast cancer cells and normal mammary epithelial cells using assays of cell viability, migration, invasion, autophagy-related responses, lysosome-associated changes, immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy, and Western blotting. Exploratory network analysis was used to prioritize candidate BBM-associated pathways, and molecular docking was used to predict interactions between BBM and selected pathway proteins. Antitumor activity was further assessed in an MCF-7 xenograft model.
