RESULTS: BBM inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of breast cancer cells while showing relatively low cytotoxicity toward normal mammary epithelial cells. BBM treatment was associated with increased levels of p-ULK1, ATG5, ATG7, and Beclin1, increased LC3 puncta, and accumulation of double-membraned autophagosomes. BBM was also associated with TFEB nuclear translocation, increased LAMP2 expression, and enhanced LysoTracker staining. Network analysis prioritized the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, and molecular docking predicted potential interactions between BBM and PI3K, Akt1, and mTOR. Western blot analysis showed reduced phosphorylation of these proteins in cultured breast cancer cells. In the MCF-7 xenograft model, BBM inhibited tumor growth and was associated with changes in autophagy-related markers. DISCUSSION: These findings support the involvement of autophagy-related responses, lysosome-associated changes, and PI3K/Akt1/mTOR pathway modulation in the anti-breast-cancer effects of BBM, while further studies are needed to establish direct target engagement and causal relationships.

articles.title: PCSK9 inhibitor use and risk of dementia and neurodegenerative diseases in adults aged 50 Years and older: a global electronic health record study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors achieve profound lipid lowering, yet their long-term neurocognitive effects remain uncertain. Evidence from randomized trials is limited by short follow-up and lack of dedicated neurodegenerative endpoints. METHODS: We performed a retrospective target trial emulation using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥50 years with hyperlipidemia initiating PCSK9 inhibitors or comparator lipid-lowering therapies between 2015 and 2024 were included. Active-comparator cohorts were constructed against statins, ezetimibe, and fenofibrate or cholestyramine with mutual exclusion of prior exposure. Propensity score matching at a 1:1 ratio balanced demographics, body mass index, socioeconomic indicators, healthcare utilization, and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Outcomes included incident all-cause dementia, Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia, Parkinson's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders. Sensitivity analyses incorporated lag periods, varying follow-up durations, alternative matching strategies, and intention-to-treat analyses. Cross-dataset validation was additionally conducted using the US Collaborative Network to assess reproducibility under independent data settings. Hazard ratio along with 95% confidence interval were evaluated in each analysis. RESULTS: Among 31,604 matched PCSK9 inhibitor-statin pairs, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower risks of all-cause dementia (HR 0.454; 95% CI 0.394-0.522), Alzheimer's disease (HR 0.553; 95% CI 0.433-0.705), vascular dementia (HR 0.536; 95% CI 0.402-0.714), Parkinson's disease (HR 0.686; 95% CI 0.544-0.865), and other neurodegenerative disorders (HR 0.730; 95% CI 0.645-0.825). Results were consistent across comparator therapies, cross-dataset validation and sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower observed risks of neurodegenerative outcomes across multiple analyses and datasets. These findings support a potential association but do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective trials.

articles.title: Early postmarketing reporting patterns of resmetirom in FAERS: disproportionality analyses with indication-restricted and active comparators.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Resmetirom is the first approved liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist for noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with fibrosis. Early liver-event reporting may be distorted by indication leakage (the treated disease or its manifestations recorded as adverse events), disease progression, and surveillance bias. METHODS: We analyzed FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 2024Q1 through 2026Q1. Deduplicated primary- or secondary-suspect reports were assessed at preferred-term, system-organ-class, and nine predefined clinical-cluster levels using frequentist and Bayesian disproportionality metrics. References included all FAERS, US MASH-indication reports, and an exploratory 144-report active comparator. Sensitivity analyses examined cirrhosis indications, serious outcomes, onset-data selection, and co-medications. RESULTS: Among 3,155,054 deduplicated cases, 1,429 resmetirom reports were analyzed. Versus all non-resmetirom reports, RORs (95% CIs) were 12.13 (10.61-13.88) for hepatocellular injury and 11.46 (9.24-14.21) for cholestasis/biliary events. Gastrointestinal, thyroid/metabolic, and rash/hypersensitivity reporting was also enriched. Hepatic estimates remained elevated after excluding 35 cirrhosis-indication reports and in restricted comparisons, although sparse cells produced wide confidence intervals. The active comparator comprised 142 GLP-1/GIP and two pioglitazone reports. Against this reference, RORs were 1.36 (0.93-1.99) for gastrointestinal intolerance, 0.93 (0.59-1.47) for nausea, 1.42 (0.18-11.18) for cholelithiasis, and 1.95 (1.12-3.41) for diarrhoea. The first three attenuated, whereas diarrhoea remained elevated. Only 206 reports (14.4%) had valid exact onset dates, with systematic differences from reports lacking dates. Sex was missing in 94.6%. Gemfibrozil and clopidogrel were co-reported in three and 25 cases, respectively. CONCLUSION: Early FAERS reporting patterns recapitulated recognized gastrointestinal, hepatic, biliary, cutaneous, and thyroid/metabolic domains. Comparator-dependent attenuation suggests that crude all-FAERS estimates partly reflect treatment-context reporting. However, the small GLP-1/GIP-dominant comparator, missing data, target-organ confounding, and spontaneous-report limitations preclude incidence, comparative-risk, or causal inference. These hypothesis-generating patterns support clinical monitoring and denominator-based confirmation.

articles.title: Protective effect of melatonin on intestinal mucosal injury in intermittent hypoxic rats.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of melatonin (MT) on intestinal mucosal injury associated with intermittent hypoxic (HI) in rats. METHODS: Thirty-six male Wistar rats were randomly divided into control (Ctrl), HI, MT groups (n = 12 per group). Each group was further divided into 2- and 4-week subgroups (n = 6 per group per time point), with different animals used at the two terminal sampling time points. Rats in the Ctrl group were exposed to compressed air, whereas rats in the HI and MT groups underwent intermittent hypoxia for 7 h daily. MT (20 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally before each daily exposure, while rats in the Ctrl and HI groups received an equivalent volume of vehicle. At the designated 2- or 4-week endpoint, the sampling procedure was initiated immediately after completion of the final daily exposure. Small intestinal tissue and central venous blood were collected. Intestinal histopathological changes were assessed by hematoxylin and eosin staining and Chiu scoring, and villus area, height, thickness, and crypt depth were measured. Serum ROS, MDA, SOD, and DAO levels were determined. RESULT: Intermittent hypoxia was associated with intestinal histopathological injury and significant reductions in villus area, villus height, villus thickness, and crypt depth at both 2 and 4 weeks. At 2 weeks, no significant differences in villus morphometric parameters were observed between the MT and HI groups, at 4 weeks, villus area and height were significantly greater in the MT group than in the HI group. At 2 weeks, SOD activity was significantly higher in the MT group than in the HI group, whereas ROS, MDA, and DAO levels did not differ significantly between these groups. At 4 weeks, the MT group showed significantly lower ROS, MDA, and DAO levels and significantly higher SOD activity than the HI group. Histological findings also indicated less severe intestinal mucosal injury in MT-treated rats. CONCLUSION: Intermittent hypoxia was associated with intestinal mucosal injury and changes in oxidative stress-related biochemical indicators in rats. Melatonin treatment was associated with attenuation of histopathological injury and a more favorable biochemical profile, with these differences being more evident at 4 weeks.

articles.title: Modulatory effect of Canavalia gladiata lectin on quinolone activity against multidrug-resistant and efflux pump-positive Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: Clinically relevant bacteria have increasingly developed resistance to antimicrobial agents, reducing the effectiveness of conventional antibiotic therapies. In this context, antibiotic adjuvants capable of restoring or enhancing the activity of existing drugs represent a potential strategy against multidrug-resistant bacteria. This study evaluated the potential of a lectin isolated from Canavalia gladiata seeds (CGL) as an antibiotic-modulating agent against multidrug-resistant and efflux pump-positive bacterial strains. CGL was purified by affinity chromatography on Sephadex G-50, and its direct antibacterial activity was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC). Its modulatory effects were subsequently assessed in combination with conventional antibiotics and in assays involving strains carrying the NorA and MepA efflux pumps. CGL showed weak intrinsic antibacterial activity against all tested strains, with MIC values ≥1,024 μg/mL. However, when used at a sub-inhibitory concentration, CGL moderately enhanced the activity of norfloxacin against Staphylococcus aureus 10, reducing the MIC from 256 to 170.6 μg/mL, and ciprofloxacin against S. aureus K2068, reducing the MIC from 32 to 13.3 μg/mL. These effects did not restore bacterial susceptibility to clinically established therapeutic breakpoints. In contrast, no significant enhancement was observed for the other antibiotic combinations, and some associations resulted in increased MIC values. Therefore, CGL does not appear to act as a direct antibacterial agent under the conditions evaluated, but may have potential as an antibiotic adjuvant, particularly in combination with quinolones against selected S. aureus strains. Further mechanistic, toxicity, and in vivo studies are required to determine its applicability as an antibiotic-modulating agent.

articles.title: Degradation-Driven Implications for the Pharmacology and Risk Profile of Fexofenadine.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Understanding a drug's degradation profile is essential for ensuring its stability, efficacy, and safety. This minireview summarizes the pharmacological characteristics of fexofenadine and predicts its degradation pathways, with an emphasis on quality assessment and regulatory implications. METHODS: To build on the outlined objectives, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus using keywords related to fexofenadine's pharmacology, chemical structure, and degradation mechanisms. Of 368 records identified, 52 studies met the inclusion criteria and were critically analyzed. RESULTS: Following this analysis, it was found that fexofenadine is susceptible to photolysis, hydrolysis, and N-nitrosation processes. DISCUSSION: Fexofenadine's vulnerabilities, which are corroborated by forced degradation studies, may compromise its stability and lead to nitrosamine formation. Notably, the drug is primarily excreted unchanged, indicating minimal metabolic transformation. Predicted metabolic routes include aromatic hydroxylation, Ndealkylation, and piperidine ring opening; however, its high polarity favors renal elimination. Phase II conjugation, particularly glucuronidation, may further contribute to its clearance and the absence of detectable metabolites. In addition, nanoformulations have been shown to enhance fexofenadine's stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic performance. CONCLUSION: Further investigation into fexofenadine's stability is critical for optimizing formulation strategies, guiding quality control, and mitigating degradation-related risks. Theoretical and experimental insights can strengthen regulatory compliance and ensure sustained drug safety.

articles.title: Ligand-modified Lipid-based Drug Delivery Vehicles for the Selective Targeting of Cancerous Cells.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy is widely recognized as the mainstay of cancer therapy; however, its lack of specificity and off-target toxicities limit therapeutic success. The lipid-based nanocarriers with targeting ligands such as folic acid, transferrin, aptamers, and antibodies are widely recognized as effective for cancer cell targeting. However, no ligand-modified lipid-based system has reached regulatory approval despite three decades of preclinical development. This review synthesizes and evaluates mechanistic, computational, and translational aspects of ligand-modified lipid nanocarriers. The review discusses lipid drug delivery systems in cancer and targeting strategies, mainly focusing on active targeting by ligands. The ligands are compared against standardized criteria, revealing no single class dominates but rather a balance of competing properties. The enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect is examined against clinical evidence. The barriers for ligand-modified lipid-based nanoparticles that can affect the ligand targeting efficiency are discussed. Given the redirected accumulation of LNPs in the liver, which leads to hepatic tropism, approaches such as biomimetics and stealth ligand modification are discussed as strategies to prolong circulation and improve therapeutic efficacy. Furthermore, applications of artificial intelligence to ligand-modified lipid nanoparticles are reviewed, with identification of gaps in application in ligand-modified LNPs. Clinically, FDA- and EMA-approved lipid formulations validate translational feasibility, though ligand-modified systems remain challenging due to manufacturing complexity and regulatory hurdles. This review uniquely integrates mechanistic, translational, and computational perspectives of ligand-modified lipid-based nanoparticle systems to bridge laboratory and preclinical innovation with clinical feasibility in cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Limonene-loaded nanoliposomes confer enhanced hepatoprotection against lipopolysaccharide-induced sepsis-like inflammatory liver injury via immunopharmacological modulation of Nrf2/HO-1, TLR4/NF-κB, and apoptotic signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition driven by dysregulated immune and inflammatory responses, leading to multi-organ dysfunction, including liver injury. This study investigated the pharmacological and toxicological effects of limonene (LM) and limonene-loaded nanoliposomes (LM-LNPs) in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced model of hepatic injury in male Albino rats. LPS caused hepatic damage marked by elevated liver enzymes, dyslipidemia, oxidative and nitrosative stress, and suppression of the Nrf2/HO-1 axis, alongside activation of TLR4/NF-κB signaling, increased cytokines, and apoptosis. Histological findings confirmed severe injury. LM treatment partially ameliorated these alterations, whereas LM-LNPs demonstrated significantly greater hepatoprotective efficacy. Specifically, LM-LNPs restored liver function biomarkers, improved lipid profiles, enhanced endogenous antioxidant defenses, and reactivated the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway, while suppressing TLR4/NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses. This resulted in reduced cytokine production, attenuated oxidative damage, and modulation of apoptosis, with preservation of hepatic architecture. Immunohistochemical analysis further confirmed upregulation of NRF2 expression and downregulation of NF-κB in hepatic tissues. Notably, nanoliposomal encapsulation improved the pharmacokinetic and biopharmaceutical properties of limonene, including controlled release, enhanced intestinal permeability, increased systemic bioavailability, and improved hepatic tissue distribution. In conclusion, LM-LNPs exert potent hepatoprotective effects against LPS-induced sepsis-like inflammatory liver injury through coordinated modulation of oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and apoptosis, highlighting their potential as a nano-enabled pharmacological strategy for managing inflammation-associated liver damage. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) Modeling to Predict Pharmacokinetic Endpoints of a Sunscreen Lotion Containing Oxybenzone.
articles.abstract: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling enables quantitative prediction of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of drug substances in virtual subjects. Its application to topical drug products, particularly sunscreens, can elucidate drug disposition within the human body, thereby supporting both product development and regulatory decision making. This study involves the development of a PBPK model for a sunscreen lotion containing oxybenzone, a widely used UV filter with documented systemic absorption. The initial PBPK model, parameterized using skin permeation data from in vitro permeation testing (IVPT), underpredicted systemic PK results following a single-dose sunscreen application in the clinical setting. Integrating the product rubbing during application into the refined PBPK model substantially improved model predictability, with prediction errors (%PE) of 19.4 and 16.4 for the geometric mean Cmax and AUC of oxybenzone, respectively. Moreover, the refined model predicted multiple-dose scenarios with %PE values of 7.1 and 6.0 for Cmax and AUC, respectively. Collectively, this study demonstrates a robust PBPK modeling approach that integrates compound properties, formulation attributes, in vitro skin permeation data, and application mechanics to accurately predict systemic oxybenzone exposure. This modeling framework provides an opportunity to support sunscreen safety assessment without extensive clinical studies. Furthermore, it establishes a foundation for PBPK modeling of other topical products where application mechanics meaningfully influence absorption.

articles.title: Influence of Material Grade and Solvent Environment on Thermoresponsive Poloxamer-Based Injectable Hydrogels.
articles.abstract: Poloxamer 407-based hydrogels are widely used in injectable drug delivery because of their thermoreversible gelation, biocompatibility, and tunable rheological properties. Although commercially available under different trade names, including Kolliphor 407 and Pluronic F127, nominally identical poloxamers may exhibit formulation-dependent differences arising from manufacturing-related variability. Understanding these differences is important for pharmaceutical formulation development. This study compared poloxamer 407 hydrogels prepared from two commercial sources, Kolliphor 407 and Pluronic F127, at concentrations of 10-30% (w/w) in purified water and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Formulations were evaluated for gelation temperature, gelation time, and the effect of mixing on thermoresponsive behavior. Mechanical properties were assessed by spreadability and adhesion testing, while pH, in vitro hydrogel dissolution, and cytotoxicity assay using NIH/3T3 fibroblast cells were performed to evaluate material suitability as injectable drug delivery systems. The two commercial grades exhibited distinct formulation characteristics. Kolliphor 407 consistently showed lower gelation temperatures than Pluronic F127 at equivalent concentrations. PBS improved the mechanical properties of Kolliphor 407 formulations, whereas Pluronic F127 was less affected by solvent composition. Cytotoxicity studies demonstrated the superior biocompatibility of PBS-based hydrogels, with 18% formulations showing no significant cytotoxicity compared with controls. Among the tested systems, the 18% Kolliphor 407 hydrogel prepared in PBS demonstrated the most favorable combination of gelation near physiological temperature, appropriate mechanical properties, and excellent biocompatibility. These findings demonstrate that material grade and solvent environment significantly influence the performance of poloxamer 407 formulations despite their nominal chemical equivalence, emphasizing the importance of material selection during the design for potential injectable application.

articles.title: Editorial: Current use of 3D printing methods in drug delivery Special Issue.
Repeated oral trazodone in male and female rats: Sex-dependent anxiolytic-like effects, altered male sexual motivation and dose-related testicular and epididymal changes in the same animals.
articles.abstract: Trazodone is a multimodal antidepressant and hypnotic used off-label for insomnia and anxiety in humans and, in veterinary medicine, as an anxiolytic and sedative in dogs and cats. In both settings it is given repeatedly, largely to individuals who are not depressed, and with little regard to sex. Its behavioural and reproductive consequences have been examined separately, in separate animals; here both were assessed in the same cohort. Male and female Wistar rats received trazodone hydrochloride at 5, 10 or 20 mg/kg/day (T5, T10, T20) or vehicle by gavage for 28 consecutive days (postnatal days 60-87; n = 6-8/group), with behavioural testing from postnatal day 88, approximately 24 h after the final dose. Open-field locomotion was unaltered in either sex; female rearing was reduced only at 20 mg/kg. In the elevated plus-maze, trazodone increased open-arm time and reduced closed-arm time in males (T5, T10) and in females (T10, T20), the effective dose range being lower in males. In an incentive-zone test, T20 males spent more time in the male-incentive zone while time near the female, approaches and latency were unchanged - a loss of directional preference rather than increased sexual interest. In the same males, blinded histomorphometry showed reduced seminiferous epithelium thickness at every dose and reduced caput epididymal luminal area and perimeter; testicular and epididymal severity scores were increased at 10 and 20 mg/kg, while gonadosomatic index, relative liver weight and hepatic scores were unchanged. The dose that altered male sexual incentive behaviour was also the dose with the most pronounced testicular change. The mechanism was not tested here and remains to be established.

articles.title: Amino acids for the treatment of Parkinson's disease: beyond levodopa.
A PK-Driven Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Model Predicts Cytokine Release Syndrome Severity Across T Cell-Activating Therapies via a Locked Cytokine Amplification Network.
articles.abstract: Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is a major dose-limiting toxicity of T cell-engaging immunotherapies. Existing CRS models are drug-class-specific; here we show that a single locked cytokine network captures CRS severity across mechanistically distinct drug classes, changing only drug-specific upstream activation parameters. We developed a PK-driven quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model linking drug exposure, T cell activation dynamics, and a macrophage-amplified cytokine network to clinical CRS severity. The 17-parameter downstream amplification network with macrophage-gated STAT3 positive feedback was calibrated on blinatumomab, structurally refined using TGN1412 as a transparently disclosed development case, then locked and tested blind on OKT3. The locked network reproduced the clinically observed CRS severity ordering across all three antibody-based T cell engager classes (bispecific, CD28 superagonist, and anti-CD3 with activation-induced cell death) without re-fitting any shared parameter. The OKT3 blind prediction passed eight qualitative plausibility checks, and its peak TNF- α  fell within values measured in patients. Tocilizumab rescue simulation reproduced five clinically validated phenomena. A mechanistic parameter swap reversing the T cell exhaustion rate between OKT3 and TGN1412 reversed CRS severity in the expected direction. Local robustness analysis (926 of 5000 parameter sets accepted, 18.5%) and a 2D stability map over the two threshold-setting parameters (0 of 900 wrong-order combinations) confirmed that the cross-drug severity ordering is a property of a feasible parameter region rather than a single tuned point. The locked model predicted three distinct dose-response shapes without re-fitting. Findings should be interpreted as a mechanistic proof-of-concept; prospective clinical validation remains pending.

articles.title: Current utilization and challenges of pediatric administration devices in China: a nationwide survey.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medical administration devices are essential for the safe and accurate delivery of pediatric medicines yet handling and dosing errors remain common in clinical practice. Whilst European surveys have documented healthcare professional (HCP) perspectives on oral and respiratory administration devices, no equivalent data exist for China. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to examine the views, practices, and experiences of Chinese hospital-based HCPs regarding oral and respiratory pediatric administration devices, and to identify challenges, age-appropriate device use, and priorities for improvement. METHODS: An electronic self-administered questionnaire, adapted from the validated EuPFI HCP survey, was distributed to pediatric HCPs across 23 provinces and municipalities in China. The survey covered device administration practices, frequency and type of devices supplied, age-appropriateness of devices, training and demonstration practices, adequacy of instructions, and reported difficulties. A total of 600 questionnaires were distributed, of which 107 valid responses were retained for oral device analysis and 104 for respiratory device analysis. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 22, GraphPad Prism 10 and WPS, with chi-square tests, Fisher's exact tests, Mann-Whitney tests, Friedman tests, and Kruskal-Wallis tests applied as appropriate. A thematic coding approach was applied to open-ended responses. A sensitivity analysis was conducted on several key data after excluding Shanghai. RESULTS: 41.1% of respondents reported routinely supplying oral administration devices to pediatric patients, compared with 87.5% for respiratory devices. In contrast to European findings where oral syringes predominate, measuring cups were the most frequently supplied oral device in China (mean 9.8 times per week versus 4.7 for oral syringes, p = 0.0009), a pattern reflected in the parallel Chinese caregiver survey. Doctors supplied oral devices significantly more frequently than pharmacists (60.0% versus 24.6%, p = 0.0003). For respiratory devices, solution for nebulization and/or nebulizer was the most frequently provided across all age groups, with facemask for inhaler or nebulizer considered appropriate from birth and dry powder inhaler emerging as the predominant device in children aged nine years and above. Age-dependent patterns of device use were broadly consistent with international recommendations. Only 15.0% of HCPs always explained or demonstrated oral device use to patients, compared with 43.3% for respiratory devices (p = 0.0036). The most frequently reported difficulties with oral devices were trouble measuring the correct dose (52.3%) and inability to identify correct graduations (41.1%), whilst for respiratory devices, instructions difficult to follow and device too complicated to use were each cited by 36.5% of respondents. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies significant gaps in oral and respiratory administration devices, type of device supplied, and training practices in Chinese pediatric hospital settings, with measuring cup dominance representing a particular patient safety concern given the established superiority of oral syringe for accurate pediatric dosing. Respiratory administration device is considerably more developed, though usability and technique-related challenges persist. Improving oral device supply standards, clarifying professional roles in device counseling, and developing culturally appropriate instructional materials are priorities for enhancing the safety of pediatric medicine administration in China. These findings complement existing European data and contribute to the growing international evidence base informing pediatric administration device development and regulatory guidance.

articles.title: Targeted Protein Degradation as a Novel Drug Discovery Platform for Antimicrobial Resistance: PROTACs, BacPROTACs, and Beyond.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) represents one of the growing global public health concerns, demanding the development of novel therapeutic modalities based on mechanisms of action different from those of conventional occupancy-based inhibitors. Targeted Protein Degradation (TPD), specifically Proteolysis- targeting Chimeras (PROTACs), provides a new concept in which bacterial proteins can be degraded rather than temporarily inhibited. In this review, we discuss the development of PROTAC technology and its potential in the field of antibacterial drug discovery. The FDA Approval of Vepdegestrant (ARV-471), the first clinically approved TPD drug, in May 2026 represents a milestone in this area. Among the approaches used for antibacterial purposes, BacPROTACs and Homo-BacPROTACs, which aim to degrade proteins in the Clp protease network in bacteria, represent strong examples of this concept and have demonstrated selective protein degradation, antibiotic resensitization, and bactericidal activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, including drug-resistant ones. These findings provide strong evidence for the feasibility of using the bacterial proteostasis network for the development of an antibacterial treatment based on protein degradation. Nevertheless, clinical translation still faces challenges due to large molecular size, poor solubility, limited permeability, kinetic limitations, cellular delivery, bacterial efflux, and limited applicability to Gramnegative pathogens. Continued innovation is needed to make antibacterial TPD clinically viable.

articles.title: Ticagrelor in the Emergency Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Comprehensive Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Acute Coronary Syndromes (ACS) - encompassing STEMI and NSTEACS - remain among the foremost causes of cardiovascular mortality worldwide. Ticagrelor, the first reversibly binding, direct-acting oral P2Y12 antagonist, has demonstrated superior efficacy over clopidogrel in landmark trials and carries a Class I recommendation in current international guidelines. This review provides a comprehensive, evidence-based appraisal of ticagrelor's pharmacology, clinical efficacy, safety, and decision- making guidance in the emergency management of ACS. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to May 2026. A narrative synthesis prioritised meta-analyses, systematic reviews, and randomised controlled trials, including PLATO, ISAR-REACT 5, TWILIGHT, TICO, PEGASUS-TIMI 54, and GLOBAL LEADERS, alongside the 2023 ESC and 2025 ACC/AHA guidelines. RESULTS: Ticagrelor significantly reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke versus clopidogrel (HR 0.84; p < 0.001) with a concomitant all-cause mortality benefit. Ticagrelor monotherapy after short dual antiplatelet therapy reduced major bleeding without increasing ischaemic events. Extended ticagrelor (60 mg twice daily) beyond 12 months reduced recurrent events in high-risk post-myocardial infarction patients. Plaque erosion pathobiology and neutrophil extracellular trap attenuation identify contexts in which ticagrelor may confer additional benefit. DISCUSSION: Regimen selection requires integrating the culprit lesion phenotype, a two-axis ischaemichaemorrhagic risk framework, and an assessment of contraindications, drug interactions, and special populations, including elderly patients, those with renal impairment, and those requiring oral anticoagulation. CONCLUSION: Ticagrelor offers potent, reversible platelet inhibition with a favourable efficacy-safety balance across the ACS spectrum. Individualised, phenotype-guided therapy optimises outcomes and minimises harm.

articles.title: Antifibrotic, Anti-inflammatory, and Antioxidant Potential of Punica granatum in Ameliorating Liver Fibrosis in Rats.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pomegranate (Punica granatum) has been recognised for its hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant qualities, but the molecular, cellular and whole-organism mechanisms underlying its anti-fibrotic qualities remain unclear. This study used an integrated in silico, in vitro and in vivo strategy to assess the antifibrotic activity of P. granatum peel extract against liver fibrosis caused by carbon tetrachloride (CCl4). METHODS: The phytochemicals from the pomegranate peel were extracted using methanol and analysed via polarity-based fractionation and spectrophotometry. The antioxidant capacity of the extract was evaluated using the DPPH method, while anti-inflammatory activity was assessed using the BSA method. In vivo, 42 male Sprague-Dawley rats were divided into 7 groups and treated with P. granatum methanol extract (PGM) alone (200 and 400 mg/kg bw) or in combination with CCl4 (1 mL/kg bw) for 6 weeks, with silymarin (100 mg/kg bw) as the hepatoprotective reference agent. Serum biochemistry, hepatic antioxidant enzymes (SOD, catalase and peroxidase), oxidative stress markers (H2O2, nitrite and TBARS), body weight, liver weight, haematology and liver histopathology (H&E) were examined.. RESULTS: In silico molecular docking of the 11 compounds showed that punicalagin exhibited the highest binding affinity to integrin and TGF-β, and it was one of the three compounds with the highest binding affinity to PDGF. PGM showed measurable antioxidant activity (DPPH IC50 = 301.13 ± 2.03 μg/mL vs. ascorbate 338.83 μg/mL) and weaker anti-inflammatory activity than aspirin (BSA IC50 = 350.6 ± 3.01 μg/mL vs. aspirin 94.37 μg/mL). CCl4 intoxication markedly increased serum ALT, AST, ALP, and bilirubin; decreased hepatic SOD, catalase, and peroxidase; increased H2O2, nitrite, and TBARS; and caused severe hepatocellular necrosis and hepatic fibrosis on histological analysis. Co-administration of PGM (200 and 400 mg/kg) significantly reversed these changes in antioxidant enzyme activities, serum and oxidative stress markers, liver and body weights, and liver histology compared with CCl4 alone, and it did not significantly affect haematological parameters. DISCUSSION: Based on the docking, biochemical, and histological results, P. granatum extract may affect fibrogenic signal transduction through integrin/PDGF/TGF-β and restore antioxidant balance in the liver in this short-term model, with no apparent adverse effects. CONCLUSION: The hepatoprotective and antioxidant activities of P. granatum peel extract against CCl4 toxicity in rats make it a promising candidate for further pharmacokinetic studies, histological studies of fibrosis and clinical trials as a hepatoprotective and antifibrotic agent.

articles.title: Integrative Genetic, Molecular Simulation, and Surface Plasmon Resonance Analysis of Shierwei Wenxiao Decoction-Related Candidate Interactions in Cystic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To integrate genetic, computational, and biophysical evidence to prioritize candidate gene-expression signals and compound-protein interactions that are potentially relevant to cystic kidney disease and the Shierwei Wenxiao Decoction. METHODS: Kidney-cortex expression Quantitative Trait Locus (eQTL) data and FinnGen R11 summary statistics were integrated through summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR), HEIDI testing, formal colocalization, and independent renal eQTL replication. A database-derived compound library was screened against protein-coding candidate targets using molecular docking. Two prioritized compound-protein pairs underwent molecular dynamics simulations, MM/GBSA binding-energy estimation, and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) assessment. RESULTS: SMR identified 13 nominal associations between gene expression and a composite cystic kidney disease phenotype (P_SMR < 0.05; P_HEIDI > 0.05), but none survived false discovery rate correction. Formal colocalization identified no robust shared causal signals under default priors, including those in the HLA region. HLA-DRB6 was reannotated as a pseudogene and excluded from protein-focused analyses, leaving nine protein-coding candidate targets. FAM118A and LDHC showed reproducible renal eQTL signals, although colocalization remained inconclusive. Docking, molecular dynamics, and SPR findings supported candidate physical interactions under the respective experimental and computational conditions. DISCUSSION: The findings provide a framework for candidate prioritization, while uncertainties in genetic causality, compound exposure, and target engagement limit mechanistic interpretation. Observed binding does not demonstrate target modulation, disease efficacy, or formula-specific pharmacological activity without direct functional validation in relevant disease models. CONCLUSION: These exploratory findings nominate genetic signals and compound-protein interactions for follow-up investigation. Independent genetic, phytochemical, functional, and disease-model studies are needed before therapeutic relevance can be established.

articles.title: The N-Nitrosamine Crisis in Antidiabetic Drugs: Toxicological Insights, Regulatory Challenges, Analytical Detection and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: The detection of carcinogenic N-nitrosamine impurities in first-line antidiabetic medicines has revealed critical vulnerabilities in pharmaceutical safety and affected patient confidence in lifelong therapies. This review links the mechanistic roots of N-nitrosamines to clinical consequences. Nitrosamines in drugs such as metformin, sitagliptin, and pioglitazone arise through interactions between susceptible amine precursors, nitrite-containing excipients, and manufacturing or storage conditions that catalyze nitrosation. Advanced analytical tools, including LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, and supercritical fluid chromatography, now enable trace-level detection, aligning with increasingly stringent international guidelines. Global regulatory agencies have transitioned from reactive recalls to proactive risk management, yet challenges persist in harmonizing acceptable intake limits and addressing nitrosamine drug substance-related impurities (NDSRIs). Importantly, this review highlights host-dependent risk modulation, including how gut microbiota and pharmacogenomic variability in CYP2E1 and CYP2A6 significantly alter nitrosamine bioactivation and carcinogenicity. These findings challenge one-size-fits-all regulatory thresholds and argue for more personalized risk models. Future progress requires integrating advanced manufacturing, next-generation analytics, and individualized risk assessment to safeguard essential diabetes medicines and restore long-term trust in pharmacotherapy.

articles.title: Corrigendum to: A Review Unveiling the Ferroptosis-Regulated Cell Signalling Pathways in Breast Cancer to Elucidate Potent Targets for Cancer Management.
articles.abstract: Following publication of the article entitled "A Review Unveiling the Ferroptosis-Regulated Cell Signalling Pathways in Breast Cancer to Elucidate Potent Targets for Cancer Management" [1], certain phrases and expressions were identified that were unclear or inconsistent with established scientific terminology. To ensure accuracy and clarity of the published record, these expressions have been corrected using appropriate terminology that more accurately conveys the intended scientific meaning. These corrections are limited to the wording and terminology of the affected passages and do not alter the data, results, scientific interpretations, or conclusions of the article. The specific correction is provided below: Section 3.3. articles.title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Extracts and Active Biomolecules of Morinda officinalis How: A Review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Global population aging and the rising burden of immunosenescencerelated disorders have created an urgent need for safe, low-toxicity immunomodulators suitable for middleaged and elderly populations. Morinda officinalis How (MO, called "Ba-Ji-Tian" in China), a traditional Chinese kidney-tonifying herb, has shown promising immunomodulatory activity. This review aims to integrate current knowledge on the multidimensional immunomodulatory functions and regulatory networks of MO extracts and their major active biomolecules and summarize their mechanistic contributions in immune-related diseases. METHODS: Peer-reviewed literature published over the past decade was comprehensively searched and systematically appraised to evaluate the in vitro and in vivo immunomodulatory effects of MO extracts and their major active constituents, including MO polysaccharides, oligosaccharides, iridoid glycosides, anthraquinones, and sterols. RESULTS: Accumulating evidence indicates that MO exerts bidirectional immunoregulation by modulating cytokine secretion, promoting the proliferation and activation of immune cells including lymphocytes and macrophages, and increasing immune organ indices. Its representative compounds, such as monotropein, rubiadin, physcion, daucosterol, and stigmasterol, contribute to these effects and help alleviate aging-related chronic inflammatory diseases. DISCUSSION: MO extracts and active biomolecules exhibit marked immunomodulatory properties. However, these findings vary across experimental models and doses, and the molecular mechanism remains incompletely defined. Standardized extracts and mechanism-oriented studies are therefore needed to support translational development. CONCLUSION: MO and its active biomolecules represent promising, mildly acting immunomodulators with considerable potential for clinical application in aging-related immune dysfunction.

articles.title: Jiangtang Pill for Type 2 Diabetes: Network Pharmacology and Transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study computationally explores the polypharmacological mechanisms of Jiangtang Pill (JTP) in treating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) using an integrated in silico approach. METHODS: Active compounds of JTP and predicted pharmacological targets were extracted from databases. Protein-protein interaction networks identified core hubs, which were intersected with DEGs from a T2DM transcriptomic dataset (GSE15932). Functional mechanisms were evaluated via GO and KEGG analyses. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT. Molecular docking and 100-ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to evaluate the predicted binding interactions and dynamic behavior of key ligand-protein complexes. RESULTS: AKT1, MAPK3, STAT3, and TNF emerged as candidate targets supported by the integrated network and transcriptomic analyses. Functional enrichment highlighted the PI3K-Akt, AGE-RAGE, and MAPK pathways. CIBERSORT analysis indicated a lower estimated abundance of CD4+ memory activated T cells in T2DM, which was inversely associated with the expression of selected targets. The 100-ns MD simulations showed that the four ligand-protein complexes remained dynamically associated throughout the trajectories, with distinct RMSD, RMSF, compactness, and hydrogen-bonding profiles for β-sitosterol and kaempferol. DISCUSSION: By integrating network pharmacology, clinical transcriptomics, and structural analyses, this study supports a hypothesis that JTP may influence metabolic and immune-related pathways involved in T2DM. CONCLUSION: These findings provide a testable computational framework for the potential multi-target actions of JTP and warrant further experimental validation.

articles.title: An effective approach for the management of men's sexual dysfunction via local administration of Sildenafil/cyclodextrin-loaded hydrogels.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to enhance the bioavailability of Sildenafil via cyclodextrin inclusion complexation and to formulate various hydrogel systems containing modified Sildenafil as an alternative, safe treatment for erectile dysfunction. SIGNIFICANCE: Oral administration of Sildenafil is accompanied by severe hypotension, making this drug contraindicated for patients with cardiac dysfunction, which may lead to fatal acute and severe hypotension. Therefore, topical and local administration is considered an option to avoid side effects accompanying oral administration. METHODS: The current work was divided into three distinct segments. First, we enhanced the solubility of sildenafil by forming and characterizing inclusion complexes with hydroxypropyl-β-CD. Secondly, hydrogels were prepared and characterized using different gelling agents, including Carbopol 940, HPMC, and Gelatin. Lastly, the selected hydrogel system was utilized for the in vivo application in participants (n = 60). The gel formulation was applied locally on the penis 0.5 h before intercourse, and both intravaginal latency time (IVLT) and International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) were monitored before and after drug application. Besides, irritation studies were conducted on rat models. RESULTS: The drug solubility and dissolution rate were markedly improved via inclusion complexation with cyclodextrin. Also, the medicated hydrogel formulations exhibited good consistency, spreadability, and homogeneity. Notably, the gel composed of HPMC, loaded with modified Sildenafil, demonstrated the fastest release rate compared to the other gelling agents. The in vivo results revealed a remarkable improvement in both erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation parameters (IVLT and IIEF-5). Also, the results showed that there is no sign of irritation upon application. CONCLUSION: The modified Sildenafil hydrogel is an alternative and safe therapy for patients suffering from erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation since this route of administration avoids severe risks accompanying oral administration.

articles.title: The cyto-genotoxic potential of dibutyl phthalate promotes DNA damage and cellular stress with altered DNA repair gene expression in Madin-Darby Bovine Kidney (MDBK) cells.
articles.abstract: Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) is a widely used plasticizer and endocrine-disrupting chemical frequently detected in polyvinyl chloride (PVC) consumer products and environmental matrices. Although there is growing evidence of its toxicological effects, data on its cyto-genotoxic potential and the resulting molecular responses in bovine renal epithelial cells are limited. The present study investigated the cytotoxic, genotoxic, and chromosomal destabilizing effects of DBP in Madin-Darby Bovine Kidney (MDBK) cells and examined the transcriptional responses of the DNA damage-associated genes OGG1 and HPRT1. MTT assay was used to determine cell viability after exposing cells to different DBP concentrations ranging from 5 to 200 µM. Cells were then treated with 25, 50 and 75 µM DBP for the alkaline comet assay, micronucleus assay and quantitative real-time PCR analysis, based on the estimated LC₅₀ value. DBP induced a concentration-dependent reduction in cell viability, with an LC₅₀ of 50 µM after 24 h of exposure. Significant dose-dependent increases (p < 0.05) were observed in DNA damage index, comet tail DNA percentage, and genomic instability index. Similarly, micronucleus and binucleated cell frequencies, and cytostasis increased significantly, whereas cytokinesis-block proliferation index (CBPI) decreased with increasing DBP concentration. The highest tested concentration (75 µM) elicited cyto-genotoxic responses comparable to the positive control group. Gene expression analysis showed that both OGG1 (5.33-fold) and HPRT1 (6.57-fold) were elevated, with higher DBP concentrations leading to increased gene expression. These findings highlight that DBP induces concentration-dependent cyto-genotoxicity and transcriptional alterations in MDBK cells, underscoring the need for safer plasticizer alternatives.

articles.title: The inhibition of tricin on human liver cytochrome P450 enzymes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tricin has attracted increasing attention due to its diverse pharmacological properties, highlighting its considerable potential for clinical application. However, its potential for drug-drug interactions (DDIs) and its inhibitory effects on human cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the effect of tricin on CYP450s. METHODS: The inhibitory effect of tricin on CYP450s was evaluated by an in vitro study using human pooled live microsomes (HLMs). Tricin, CYP450 enzymes, and the corresponding substrates were co-incubated with HLMs using a NADPH-generating system, and the HLMs incubated without tricin or positive inhibitors served as the negative control. Corresponding inhibitory parameters were obtained by incubating tricin (0-100 µM) with the specific substrates at different concentrations. RESULTS: Tricin showed a selective inhibitory effect on the activities of CYP1A2, 2D6, and 3A4, with the IC50 values of 12.760 µM, 14.050 µM, and 6.925 µM for CYP3A4 with testosterone as substrate, and 8.070 µM for CYP3A4 with midazolam as substrate, respectively. It was revealed that tricin competitively inhibited the activities of CYP1A2 (Ki=5.641 µM) and 2D6 (Ki=6.247 µM) while non-competitively inhibited the activity of CYP3A4 (Ki=2.876 µM). The activity of CYP3A4 was also inhibited by tricin in a time-dependent inhibition (TDI) manner with a KI of 1.418 µM and a Kinact of 0.029 min⁻¹. CONCLUSIONS: In vitro HLM study indicated the competitive inhibition of tricin on CYP1A2 and 2D6, while non-competitive inhibition and TDI on CYP3A4, thereby informing its potential for clinical drug interactions. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Trastuzumab-conjugated Docetaxel-loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carriers for Gastric Cancer.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancers overexpressing human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) (10-20% of cases) are often associated with aggressive disease and poorer clinical outcomes. Trastuzumab (TZM), a HER2-specific monoclonal antibody, and docetaxel (DTX), a microtubule-stabilizing agent, are established therapies for gastric cancer, with their combination demonstrating efficacy in HER2-positive cases. Nanotechnology enables co-administration of antibodies and drugs, improving control over delivery and prolonging retention within tumors. This study aimed to develop DTX-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLC) covalently conjugated to TZM for local treatment of HER2-positive gastric cancer. Carbodiimide-mediated conjugation was verified by light-scattering and spectroscopic techniques, and the bound antibody was estimated using a colorimetric assay. The conjugated NLC were characterized for their physicochemical properties, stability, drug incorporation, morphology, in vitro release, and in vitro cytotoxicity against AGS (HER2-negative) and NCI-N87 (HER2-positive) cells. The results suggest successful TZM conjugation, yielding stable nanoconjugates that efficiently entrapped the drug and sustained its release. The conjugated DTX-loaded NLC slightly enhanced cytotoxicity in NCI-N87 cells at 10 nM compared with the unconjugated counterparts, but not in AGS cells at any concentration tested. Altogether, these findings point to the potential of the developed nanoconjugate in the context of HER2-positive gastric cancer.

articles.title: Engineering a Solid Dispersion-Integrated Fast-Dissolving Oral Film of Nicardipine Hydrochloride for Rapid Delivery in Hypertensive Urgency.
articles.abstract: Nicardipine hydrochloride (NCH) is considered an ideal treatment for hypertensive crises, particularly for the management of hypertensive urgency. NCH is a BCS class II drug with limited solubility and exhibits significant first-pass metabolism upon oral administration, which increases the daily dosing frequency. Therefore, the study focuses on developing and evaluating an NCH-solid dispersion (NCHSD) loaded oral fast-dissolving film (OSD-ODF) for the treatment of hypertensive urgency. The NCHSD was prepared by the solvent-casting method using PVP K90 as the carrier at a 1:3 drug-to-carrier ratio. The solubility of NCH was increased by a factor of 23. The NCHSD released 86.0 ± 12.6% of the drug within 6 min. A central composite design was employed to optimize OSD-ODF, with HPMC E6 and PEG 400 concentrations as variables and disintegration time, drug content, weight variation, and tensile strength as responses. A fast disintegration and rapid-release profile were achieved for the optimized ODF with a disintegration time of 88 ± 3.14 s and 104.73 ± 2.00% drug release within 1 min. The in vitro cellular study demonstrated cytocompatibility of optimized ODF in Caco-2 and NIH 3T3 cells. The findings of the cellular permeability study in Caco-2 cells revealed a significant enhancement of the permeability coefficient (p ≤ 0.05) for optimized ODF, about 9 times greater permeability than pure NCH dispersion. This suggests successful development of NCHSD-loaded optimized ODF with better solubility, fast disintegration, rapid release profile, adequate mucoadhesion and biocompatibility. The findings of this work conclude that the prepared OSD-ODF holds excellent potential and is safe for the treatment of hypertensive urgency.
